sources.news_title: The Best 2026 Oscars Red Carpet Fashion Updates, Live from ‘Marie Claire’ Editors
sources.text:
Every 2026 award show—the Golden Globes, the Actor Awards, and the BAFTAs—has led to this moment: Welcome to the 2026 Oscars red carpet. The celebrity guest list is finalized, Oscar statuettes are polished, and host Conan O’Brien is rehearsing his monologue as we speak. But wait: Before the lights dim inside the Dolby Theatre, Marie Claire is here to deliver the best live red carpet fashion updates.
As a Marie Claire celebrity fashion expert by day and award-season superfan by night, trust me when I say the 98th Annual Academy Awards will deliver standout fashion moments. Best Actress winners alone have consistently made it a night to remember, from Barbra Streisand’s naked dress in 1961 to Gwyneth Paltrow’s pink Ralph Lauren gown in 1999 and Halle Berry’s sheer Elie Saab dress in 2002. There may not be a dress code (unlike the newly-renamed Actor Awards), but preceding Oscar winners have set a high bar for modern-day nominees.
This year’s class of Best Actress hopefuls—Emma Stone, Jessie Buckley, Rose Byrne, Renate Reinsve, and Kate Hudson—is certainly up to the red-carpet task. On the fashion front, each nominee has a fighting chance of ending up on senior news editor Halie LeSavage’s post-Oscars best-dressed list. I’m also scanning the red carpet for Best Supporting Actress nominees, including Teyana Taylor, Elle Fanning, Wunmi Mosaku, Amy Madigan, and Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas. Taylor, for one, is a sartorial wildcard, after wearing Schiaparelli, Thom Browne, Burberry, and Ashi Studio this season. Then there’s Mosaku, who could decorate her growing baby bump in any number of major designers.
Regardless of who takes home an Oscar, the evening is set up to make fashion history. Plus, ABC’s broadcast, streaming live on Hulu, will begin an hour earlier this year: 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT. Marie Claire’s red carpet coverage won’t stop with the official red carpet, either. Even after the final award is presented, I’ll switch gears to the 2026 Vanity Fair Oscar Watch party, where the style plot twists will keep on coming.
For now, my fellow editors and I will share to-the-minute updates on the 2026 Oscars red carpet fashion. That includes raw, honest reactions, too…
How to Watch the 2026 Oscars Red Carpet Live
"Long before O’Brien’s hosting gig begins streaming on Hulu at 7 p.m. ET/4 p.m. PT, Chicken Shop Date star Amelia Dimoldenberg will return as the Oscars red carpet’s official correspondent. The pre-show presentation even has a name this year: On the Red Carpet at the Oscars. Beginning at 3:30 p.m. ET/12:30 p.m. PT, she’ll zoom in on the buzziest looks and interview your favorite stars, while Marie Claire listens closely for any designer details. Hulu will house the red carpet coverage, too, so no need to switch channels at all tonight."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Your 2026 Oscars Red Carpet Fashion Cheat-Sheet
"From now until the 7 p.m. ET broadcast begins (and sometimes after, if Kylie Jenner is fashionably late again), a constant stream of corsets, naked dresses, and Spring 2026 color trends will likely dominate the Dolby Theatre’s red carpet. I’ve already established Best Actress nominees as ones to watch. The Best Supporting Actress category is equally stacked with style muses, including Teyana Taylor, Wunmi Mosaku, Amy Madigan, Elle Fanning, and Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas. I have the utmost fashion faith in Taylor, especially after her bejeweled butt cleavage at the Golden Globes and her anatomically-correct Thom Browne gown at the Actor Awards. She’s worn the buzziest maisons this award season, but the One Battle After Another star keeps coming back to Schiaparelli. Daniel Roseberry’s Spring 2026 Couture and Fall 2026 womenswear collections are ripe for Taylor’s taking."
"Not only is Taylor a first-time nominee, she’ll also make her Oscars debut. Chase Infiniti, Wunmi Mosaku, Arden Cho, and more will also walk the historic red carpet for the first time. Expect them to go all-out for their debuts, whether it be with a vintage or fresh-from-the-runway pull.
Meanwhile, Oscars regulars like Emma Stone, Gwyneth Paltrow, Elle Fanning, and Kate Hudson will likely stick to what works best: glamorous gowns from their favorite ateliers. I, for one, can’t wait to see which shade Louis Vuitton loyalist Stone went with. So far this season, she’s pulled off lavender and butter yellow at the Actor Awards and Golden Globes, respectively."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Dior’s Pre-Oscars Party Set a Stylish Tone—and Teased Surprise Celebrity Guests
"Three days before the 2026 Oscars, Dior and W Magazine gathered nominees, former winners, and fashion girls alike for an invite-only dinner. The dress code? Jonathan Anderson’s Dior, of course.
Most attendees—including Priyanka Chopra, Tracee Ellis Ross, Emily Ratajkowski, and Teyana Taylor—sourced Anderson’s first two Dior collections. Perhaps he’s reserving his 12-day-old Fall 2026 line for the real deal on Sunday.
Meanwhile, fans (myself included) were most shocked to see Hailey Bieber and Kendall Jenner on the guest list: The two have famously never walked the Oscars red carpet. Seeing them in Dior—Jenner in a circa-1998 camisole and Bieber in Anderson’s reimagined Bar Jacket—made me wish for their debuts this year. I also wasn’t expecting Emma Watson’s grand return to Hollywood. If the Dior party hinted Watson will attend the 2026 Oscars, it’ll be her first ceremony since 2014."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Amelia Dimoldenberg Is the 2026 Oscars Hostess With the Mostest
"Chicken Shop Date star Amelia Dimoldenberg is the Oscars' red carpet correspondent for a third year in a row. She arrived before the biggest names in Hollywood, dressed in a strapless, black A-line gown, featuring an oversize bow at the back. Its classic simplicity allowed her diamond, collar-style necklace and matching hoop earrings to take center stage."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
'KPop Demon Hunters' Star Arden Cho Makes Her Oscars Debut
"KPop Demon Hunters is nominated for Best Animated Feature, meaning your favorite Huntrix members will grace the Oscars red carpet soon. Arden Cho, aka Rumi, was the first of the trio to arrive, dressed in Spring 2026 couture from Korean designer Miss Sohee. A strapless, black gown—with lace and fishnet naked elements—served as the base of her look. For extra drama, the actor slipped on the most voluminous of floor-length sleeves. Their moss green hue was especially eye-catching."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Bella Thorne Flaunts the First (of Many) Oscars Naked Dresses
"If the 2026 Oscars are anything like the 2026 Golden Globes, tonight will be a naked dress showdown. Bella Thorne kickstarted the trend in a long-sleeve, black Gucci gown. The brand's double-G monogram decorated Thorne's nearly-naked underlay, before a boatneck, feather-cuffed bodice made it a touch more wintery."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
2026 Oscars Red Carpet Trend Watch
"It's early in the night, but there are a few trends I'm keeping a close eye on. After the Golden Globes filled with elegant black dresses, I'm expecting the Oscars to swerve toward bolder jewel tones or pearlescent white—ending the season on a bright note. I'm also hearing feather-trims are going to swish onto the red carpet via sleeves, embellished hems, and more."—Halie LeSavage, senior fashion news editor
Hudson Williams Skates Onto the 2026 Oscars Red Carpet—and My Best-Dressed List
"My man (read: Hudson Williams) has blessed the 2026 Oscars with his sartorial prowess—for the first time ever, might I add. Following his pre-Oscars naked shirt this weekend, the Heated Rivalry star posed in an oppositely full-coverage Balenciaga suit. (According to E! News, he's been doing yoga in his look all day.) He frosted the satin lapel of his black tuxedo jacket with a diamond Serpenti brooch from Bulgari. Just a few inches south appeared a matching Serpenti watch. He's a star, ladies and gentlemen!"—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
McKenna Grace, Well, Graces the 2026 Oscars Red Carpet
"When I caught McKenna Grace walking out of her limo, I thought of Grace Kelly. Her peony-pink dress and matching, floor-length stole were a page neatly torn from the Old Hollywood playbook."—Halie LeSavage, senior fashion news editor
Rose Byrne Blooms at the 2026 Oscars Red Carpet
"When I spoke with Best Actress nominee Rose Byrne ahead of the 2026 Actor Awards, she told me she's spent red carpet season chasing 'elegance' with every look. She more than delivered at the Academy Awards in a black strapless Dior gown set with beaded lilies. To me, it looks like a woman getting her flowers and wearing them, too."—Halie LeSavage, senior fashion news editor
Renate Reinsve Sprouts a Spring 2026 Color Trend at the Oscars
"The tomato red color trend didn't just germinate on Spring 2026 runways from Bottega Veneta, Calvin Klein, Dior, Chanel, and Fendi. Best Actress nominee Renate Reinsve gave the shade a proper Hollywood close-up at the 2026 Oscars in a strapless gown. The design was as sharp as it was sultry, thanks to a hip-high cutout and high-low train. I, for one, hope more attendees follow her tomato-y lead tonight."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Misty Copeland Pirouettes at the 2026 Oscars in the Tutu Trend
"Professional ballerina Misty Copeland is slated to perform en pointe at the 2026 Oscars. Before then, she endorsed the burgeoning tutu trend on the Oscars red carpet. A shoulder-padded, plunge blazer made up the top-half of her gown. Then, her stark white skirt served as a blank canvas for a tiered lace tutu. Extra points for her subtle jewelry from Jared. Copeland's step-and-repeat comes just days after Kaia Gerber tested the tutu revival in Givenchy. Perhaps the silhouette is Hollywood's way of proving to Timothée Chalamet that ballet is still very much 'alive.'"—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Chase Infiniti's Love Affair With Lavender Continues at the Oscars
"Four days ago, Chase Infiniti attended Vanity Fair's pre-Oscars 'A Night for Young Hollywood' party in a lavender Carolina Herrera skirt set. Turns out, she was teasing her 2026 Oscars gown. Tonight, she showed out in a custom lavender Louis Vuitton gown, featuring a halter-neck bodice and ruffled tiers atop the carpet-grazing train."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
"ICE OUT" Protests Continue at the 2026 Oscars Red Carpet
"It started at the 2026 Golden Globes, continued at New York Fashion Week, and made it all the way to the Oscars red carpet: Stars have been raising their voices against abuses by ICE with 'ICE OUT' pins and pointed accessories. Glennon Doyle's bedazzled clutch summed up the movement in seven letters."—Halie LeSavage, senior fashion news editor
GapStudio Makes Its Oscars Red Carpet Debut
"Zac Posen has been steadily elevating GapStudio's profile with every red carpet. After dressing stars for everything from the ESPYs to major fashion week parties, he secured a sculpted corset gown for Barbie Ferreira on the Oscars red carpet. This blue hits even better than a great pair of jeans."—Halie LeSavage, senior fashion news editor
'KPop Demon Hunters' Stars Channel the Film's Nominated Song
"KPop Demon Hunters' breakout hit, 'Golden' scored a Best Original Song nomination at the 2026 Oscars. Leading ladies EJAE and Audrey Nuna paid homage to the chart-topping record in metallic gold. For EJAE, gold sequins cascaded from her strapless neckline onto a fringed train. Nuna walked the red carpet minutes later, in a voluminous Thom Browne ballgown. I could write a song about its gold-to-black ombré alone."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Consider Us on Zendaya Watch...
"Celebrity power stylist—I mean, image architect—Law Roach is in the building! I'm crossing my fingers and toes that his star client, Zendaya, is close behind. She hasn't attended the Academy Awards since 2024, when she wore custom Armani Privé. Personally, I'd love to see her recent bridal white streak get the Oscars treatment."—Halie LeSavage, senior fashion news editor
Odessa A'Zion Trades a Red Carpet Gown for Trophy-Worthy Trousers
"I feel so seen by Odessa A'Zion in Valentino at the 2026 Oscars: She arrived in oversize black trousers and an equally-baggy wrap top, aka the elevated version of my Oscars look right now. It's her second pro-pants pick of the current award season, following her circa-Fall 2015 Armani Privé jumpsuit at the 2026 Actor Awards."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Wunmi Mosaku Makes My Oscars Watch Party Gasp
"As soon as Wunmi Mosaku arrived at the 2026 Oscars, everyone in my watch party gasped. Who wouldn't be in awe of the first-time nominee in emerald green sequins? The off-the-shoulder, long-sleeve look hugged her growing baby bump elegantly."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Feathers Cover Every Square Inch of Demi Moore's Oscar Gown
"This time last year, Demi Moore attended the 2025 Oscars in head-to-toe silver sequins. Tonight, the Landman star traded sequins for peacock-inspired Gucci feathers, which fanned out atop her cinched bodice. According to Moore's stylist, Brad Goreski, 'Demi wanted to wear something that was a work of art.' The tufts turned mossy green around her waist, before becoming iridescent atop the mermaid train."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Jessie Buckley Tests a "Controversial" Color Combination at the 2026 Oscars
"Spring 2026 is the season of unique color combinations. Need proof? See Best Actress nominee Jessie Buckley's custom Chanel gown at the Oscars. Fashion features editor Emma Childs called the moment 'controversial.' The pleated, off-the-shoulder bodice was tomato red, contrary to the baby pink elongated skirt. I'll be channeling this red-and-pink color palette all spring long."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Zoe Saldaña Elevates the Naked Dress Trend at the Oscars
"An actor's Oscars gown doesn't need to be completely transparent to classify as 'naked.' Exhibit A: Zoe Saldaña's little black slip dress. Only the lacy balconette bodice atop her satin slip was sheer."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Teyana Taylor in Custom Chanel Leaves 'Marie Claire' Editors Speechless
"Teyana you have simply GOT to be JOKINGGGG."—Julia Marzovilla, fashion e-commerce editor
"My co-worker, Julia, took the words right out of my mouth. Teyana Taylor has delivered hit after hit this award season, and absolutely no misses. Her custom Chanel Oscars gown undeniably continued her red carpet streak. Black and white feathers down the carpet-grazing train were the cherry on top of Taylor's glamorous cake."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Kylie Jenner Ends Her Noir Gown Streak in Red-Hot Schiaparelli
"I love a classic Kylie moment, and her Oscars look really delivered. While it’s still too early to see if she’ll walk the red carpet (fingers crossed!), I’ll be satisfied with any peak into her look on film’s biggest night.”—Julia Marzovilla, fashion e-commerce editor
Kate Hudson Brings Her Mom, Goldie Hawn, as Her Oscars Plus-One
"If I was nominated for my first Academy Award, my mom would certainly be my plus-one. Clearly, Kate Hudson is as much her mother's daughter as me: The Best Actress nominee arrived at the Oscars in a peplum Armani Privé gown. (Marie Claire predicted she'd choose Armani Privé in late January, when she attended the maison's Paris Haute Couture Week show.) Goldie Hawn's black, glittery gown matched her daughter's glamour with ease."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
I Give You...Elle Fanning, a Givenchy Princess
"Elle Fanning was the picture of a princess in a Givenchy by Sarah Burton gown, fit with a strapless bodice, tulle ball skirt, and hand-stitched lavender-tinted wisteria petals. Plus, there’s a heartfelt detail to the Sentimental Value star’s look we wouldn’t know if the Best Supporting Actress nominee didn’t take the time for a quick chat with a red carpet correspondent: Fanning revealed that Burton’s a 'dear friend' and that 'she and her team sewed every wisteria petal.' The perks of being famous and having famous friends!"—Emma Childs, fashion features editor
Emma Stone's Cap-Sleeve Oscars Gown Is Classic Emma-Core
"If you made me close my eyes and draw a picture of what Emma Stone would wear to the Oscars, it would be this exact dress. She's spent all of 2026 so far wearing every possible combination of 'beaded column dress.' The look always works for her, but I'd love to see her take a risk at the after parties."—Kelsey Stiegman, contributing fashion writer
Nicole Kidman Maximizes the Oscars Feather Trend in Custom Chanel
"Following Teyana Taylor, Demi Moore, and Bella Thorne's lead, Nicole Kidman walked the Oscars red carpet in custom feather-trimmed Chanel. The bespoke peplum gown began with green and ivory sequins. Powder pink feathers became more concentrated toward the strapless dress's floor-length gown. Its elegance was only amplified by a vintage Omega Sapphette timepiece from 1966. As Omega's ambassador, she had an all-access pass to the brand's archives."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Wait—Did You See Gwyneth Paltrow's Never-Ending Slit?
"When Gwyneth Paltrow first graced the 2026 Oscars red carpet, I thought her strapless Armani Privé dress was classically glamorous. Then, she showcased its side profile, and it became one of the evening's riskiest selects. Cut-outs on either side of the dress cascaded all the way up to her neckline. To quote my co-worker, fashion features editor Emma Childs, it was 'neo-naked dressing' at its finest."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
"Gwyneth Paltrow has always been on my personal best-dressed list, but this awards season has taken my love for her style to a different level. Tonight’s custom Giorgio Armani dress (and its daring cutouts) is so chic and sexy at the same time. Obsessed.”—Julia Marzovilla, fashion e-commerce editor
Amy Madigan Didn't Accept Her First Oscar Alone
"When Amy Madigan took center stage to accept her first Oscar, I couldn't help but admiring the timepiece a few inches from the trophy. Underneath the feathered cuffs of her Dior jacket emerged a $20,600 watch from Omega, featuring 46 bezel-set diamonds."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
Anne Hathaway Attends Her First Oscars in Over a Decade
"Without sounding trite, Anne Hathaway’s look served Old Hollywood glamour on tonight’s carpet. Her stunning floral gown was so timeless, right down the velvet elbow-length gloves. Add in a half-up-half-down hairstyle and glowing makeup, and you’ve got a best-dressed look for the ages.”—Julia Marzovilla, fashion e-commerce editor
Anna Wintour and Anne Hathaway Meet On the Oscars Stage
"Two months before The Devil Wears Prada 2 hits theaters, Anne Hathaway and Anna Wintour brought the fashion drama to life at the Oscars. Marie Claire editors adored their commitment to the bit."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer
"Didn't expect the Anne and Anna link up."—Emma Childs, fashion features editor
Final Oscars Thoughts Before the 'Vanity Fair' Oscar Party
"It’s Matthieu Blazy for Chanel’s world, and we’re all just living in it—Teyana Taylor, included. The One Battle After Another star’s Chanel naked dress, fit with black and white feather fringe and silver sparkle stripes, represented exactly why newly-appointed creative director is earning such buzz. It was classic yet modern, a spotlight on craftsmanship but not stuffy, and, crucially, pure joy. Taylor was, by and large, my best-dressed of the night."—Emma Childs, fashion features editor
"I've never had an easier time putting together a best-dressed list. Tonight's nominees really showed out, from honoring Hollywood history to remixing familiar house codes. My top three? Teyana Taylor, Jessie Buckley, and Elle Fanning."—Halie LeSavage, senior fashion news editor
"Wow, what a night. For me, few award shows were nearly as exhilarating as the 2026 Oscars. Even before the broadcast began, red carpet regulars like Emma Stone, Demi Moore, and Anne Hathaway made my jaw drop in Louis Vuitton, Chanel, and Valentino, respectively. My biggest rounds of applause go to Oscars debuts from Odessa A'Zion, Chase Infiniti, and Wunmi Mosaku. Each newcomer's step-and-repeat stole the show. I'm still not over Mosaku's ability to pull of every color in the rainbow. Bravo, Oscars guests, bravo."—Meguire Hennes, fashion staff writer

sources.news_title: 'One Battle After Another' takes best picture. Here's the full list of Oscar winners
sources.text:
'One Battle After Another' takes best picture. Here's the full list of Oscar winners
One Battle After Another took home best picture at the 98th Oscars on Sunday night.
It was a big night for director Paul Thomas Anderson, who also won best director and best adapted screenplay for the film. Cassandra Kulukundis, casting director of One Battle After Another, won the Academy's first-ever award for achievement in casting.
But the wins were spread out: Sinners writer and director Ryan Coogler won his first Oscar for best original screenplay, and actor Michael B. Jordan won his first, best actor, for playing twins — Smoke and Stack — in the vampire movie. Jessie Buckley won best actress for her role as Agnes Shakespeare in Hamnet.
The ceremony even featured a tie between two live action short films: The Singers and Two People Exchanging Saliva. The last Oscar tie was in 2013, when Zero Dark Thirty and Skyfall tied in the sound editing category.
Occasionally those on stage gestured toward the world beyond Hollywood: "No to war and free Palestine," Javier Bardem said on stage, presenting the award for best international feature film.
David Borenstein, co-director of winning feature documentary Mr. Nobody Against Putin, said in his acceptance speech, "Mr. Nobody Against Putin is about how you lose your country. And what we saw when working with this footage … it's that you lose it through countless small, little acts of complicity. When we act complicit, when a government murders people on the streets of our major cities, when we don't say anything, when oligarchs take over the media and control how we can produce it and consume it, we all face a moral choice."
Co-director Pavel "Pasha" Talankin, who shot footage for the documentary while working at a Russian school, said onstage, "In the name of our future, in the name of all of our children, stop all of these wars now."

sources.news_title: Oscars 2026: Michael B. Jordan pulls off historic win
sources.text:
One Battle After Another took home best picture winner, but a huge award was taken home by Michael B. Jordan, who earned his first Academy Award on Sunday night, winning best actor for his dual performance as twins Smoke and Stack in Ryan Coogler’s Sinners, the blockbuster vampire allegory reframing America’s racial history. It was Jordan’s first nomination — and a breakthrough in a category where only five Black men had previously won. Jordan topped a formidable slate that included Timothée Chalamet, Ethan Hawke, Wagner Moura, and Leonardo DiCaprio, defying early-season odds that had favored Moura and Chalamet. His victory at the Actor Awards earlier this month signaled a late surge, and the Oscars confirmed it. The win adds to Sinners’ growing haul. With 16 nominations, the film is now the most‑nominated title in Academy history.
The ceremony also marked a milestone for K‑pop. “Golden,” from KPop Demon Hunters, became the first K‑pop song ever to win both a Grammy and an Oscar. Before their speech was abruptly cut off, Ejae managed to share a brief reflection: “Growing up everyone made fun of me for liking K‑pop. And now everyone is singing our song.” She added that the track isn’t about fame — “it’s about resilience.”
What to Know:
- One Battle After Another and Sinners dominated the ceremony, each collecting top‑tier awards and driving the night’s suspense.
- Paul Thomas Anderson won best director and adapted screenplay, adding supporting actor, casting, and editing wins to his film’s haul.
- Ryan Coogler’s Sinners secured four Oscars — original screenplay, best actor, cinematography, and score.
- Michael B. Jordan became the first performer ever honored for dual roles, playing twins Smoke and Stack.
- Autumn Durald Arkapaw became the first woman and first Black cinematographer to win the category, asking all the women in the Dolby Theatre to stand during her speech.
- Anderson used his writing win to address the world his children will inherit, calling for “common sense and decency.”
- Coogler credited his cast, studio, and family for believing in him.
- Cassandra Kulukundis won the first‑ever Oscar for casting, upsetting favorite Francine Maisler.
- Sean Penn won supporting actor for One Battle After Another; Amy Madigan earned supporting actress for Weapons in a late‑career triumph.
- KPop Demon Hunters won best animated feature, with director Maggie Kang dedicating the win to Koreans worldwide.
- Frankenstein claimed three awards — costume design, makeup and hairstyling, and production design — aided by a cheeky Devil Wears Prada 2 promo moment from Anne Hathaway and Anna Wintour.
- The live‑action short category ended in a two‑way tie between Two People Exchanging Saliva and The Singers, prompting an awkward attempt by producers to move things along.
- Billy Crystal honored Rob Reiner, and Barbra Streisand paid tribute to Robert Redford, underscored by the message, “Art can lead change.”
- All the Empty Rooms won short doc; Mr. Nobody Against Putin took feature documentary.
- Conan O’Brien opened with a drag parody of Weapons’ Aunt Gladys, earning a standing ovation.
This live blog is now closed.

‘One battle after another’ closes out the 98th Oscars with six wins
Paul Thomas Anderson’s One Battle After Another ended the night as the dominant force at the 98th Academy Awards, taking home six Oscars, including best picture and best director — a career‑defining sweep that firmly cements Anderson among the most influential filmmakers of his era. His political epic about authoritarianism and civic resistance also claimed trophies for adapted screenplay, supporting actor (Sean Penn), casting, and editing.
Ryan Coogler’s Sinners remained close on its heels, finishing with four wins for original screenplay, score, cinematography, and Michael B. Jordan’s historic best actor victory. Jordan’s dual performance as twins Smoke and Stack marked the first time an actor has ever won an Oscar for playing two roles in the same film. He thanked Coogler and Warner Bros. for “betting on original ideas and original artistry.”
The night also delivered a landmark behind the camera: Autumn Durald Arkapaw became the first woman — and first Black cinematographer — to win the category, asking every woman in the Dolby Theatre to stand as she dedicated the moment to those who helped her reach it.
Anderson used his screenplay speech to strike a political note, telling his children he hoped their generation would bring “common sense and decency” to a world his own had left in disarray. Coogler, accepting his writing award earlier in the night, thanked his cast, collaborators, and family for giving him the confidence to pursue the film.
The ceremony also marked the Academy’s first‑ever casting Oscar, awarded to Cassandra Kulukundis for assembling the sprawling ensemble of One Battle After Another, an upset over favorite Francine Maisler (Sinners).
Other major moments included Amy Madigan’s late‑career supporting actress win for Weapons, KPop Demon Hunters taking best animated feature, and Frankenstein sweeping three craft categories. A rare tie in live‑action short, a heartfelt in‑memoriam led by Billy Crystal and Barbra Streisand, and a Conan O’Brien cold‑open in full Aunt Gladys drag rounded out a ceremony that mixed spectacle, history, and a few awkward stumbles.

Autumn Durald Arkapaw makes Oscars history and dedicates win to future filmmakers
Autumn Durald Arkapaw, now the first woman and the first Black cinematographer to win the Academy Award in her category, admitted in the press room that she spent her walk to the stage worrying about one thing: time. “Are they going to kick me off?” she remembered thinking. Instead, she delivered one of the night’s most grounded and generous speeches — one aimed squarely at the next generation.
“A lot of little girls who look like me will sleep really well tonight because they’ll want to become cinematographers,” she said, calling the moment bigger than any single trophy.
During her speech, she asked every woman in the Dolby Theatre to stand, explaining later that “moments like this don’t happen without women standing up for you and advocating for you.” The gesture underscored her belief that her win represents a collective breakthrough, not just a personal milestone.
“This isn’t about me anymore,” she said. “It’s about so much more, and I wanted it for all of the ladies in the room — and for all the girls at home.”

What is ‘Sentimental Value’ about?
Joachim Trier’s Sentimental Value has emerged as one of 2025’s most acclaimed international dramas, a quietly devastating family story centered on two sisters reconnecting with their estranged father. Led by Renate Reinsve, Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas, and Stellan Skarsgård, with Elle Fanning in a key supporting role, the film traces the emotional fallout of abandonment, artistic ambition, and inherited trauma as the family reunites after years of distance.
Premiering in competition at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival, the film drew immediate praise for its precision and emotional clarity, ultimately winning the Grand Prix. Its September release in Norway cemented its status as one of Trier’s most resonant works, blending intimate character study with the director’s signature psychological nuance.
The awards response has been sweeping. Sentimental Value earned major nominations at the 83rd Golden Globes, where Skarsgård won for supporting actor, and went on to secure nine nominations at the 98th Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actress, and dual supporting actress nods for Fanning and Lilleaas.
At its core, the film follows a fractured family forced to confront old wounds: a father whose career eclipsed his responsibilities, daughters carrying the weight of his absence, and a home filled with memories both cherished and painful. As the characters circle one another — through grief, resentment, and the possibility of reconciliation — Trier crafts a drama that feels both deeply Norwegian and universally human.

Who is the president of the Academy Awards?
Producer Lynette Howell Taylor officially stepped into the role of President of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences in July 2025, succeeding Janet Yang and becoming the organization’s top elected leader for the 2025–2026 term. A veteran filmmaker with credits including A Star Is Born, Blue Valentine, Captain Fantastic, and The Accountant, Howell Taylor now oversees the Academy’s Board of Governors while Bill Kramer continues to run day‑to‑day operations as CEO.
Her election marks a return to familiar territory: Howell Taylor previously served as a Vice President and chaired the Awards Committee, and she produced the 92nd Oscars in 2020. Now, she’s tasked with guiding the Academy through a rapidly shifting industry — one grappling with evolving distribution models, labor upheaval, and viewership that has dipped and only recently begun to rebound.

What is ‘Mr. Nobody Against Putin’ about
Mr Nobody Against Putin has quickly become one of the most talked‑about documentaries of 2025, offering an unfiltered look at how the Russian government sought to shape public perception during the ongoing war in Ukraine. Directed by David Borenstein and Pavel Talankin, the film follows Talankin’s work at a school in Karabash, a struggling mining town near the Ural Mountains, where he quietly recorded the state’s expanding demands for “patriotic displays” and government‑approved lessons.
Shot over two years, the documentary captures the moment when schools were ordered to upload footage proving compliance with Kremlin messaging — a requirement that gave Talankin cover to film meetings, classroom sessions, and officials without raising suspicion. As surveillance around him intensified, he ultimately fled Russia in 2024 with the help of the filmmakers and international partners.
The film premiered at Sundance, winning a Special Jury Award, and went on to claim major honors, including the BAFTA for Best Documentary and the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature. Critics praised its rare undercover access and Talankin’s courage, with outlets like IndieWire, The Guardian, Variety, and The Daily Beast highlighting its clarity and urgency. Some reviewers noted its narrow focus on a single school, but the consensus remained overwhelmingly positive.
With a perfect score on Rotten Tomatoes and strong festival momentum, Mr Nobody Against Putin stands as a stark, human‑scale portrait of life inside an increasingly controlled Russia — and of one man’s determination to document the truth before it disappeared.

“Which country could people get killed for free speech?” he asked, pausing just long enough for the audience to brace for a geopolitical jab. Instead, he delivered a two‑beat zinger: “Let’s just leave it at North Korea and CBS.”

Jimmy Kimmel returns to the Oscars after a turbulent year off-air
Jimmy Kimmel’s surprise appearance on the Oscars stage — joking, “Wait, am I not hosting?” — came at the end of one of the most dramatic years of his career. The late‑night host, who has helmed the ABC telecast four times, spent part of the fall suspended after ABC and Disney pulled Jimmy Kimmel Live! in September over remarks he made following the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk.
The suspension was loudly celebrated by President Donald Trump, but the move backfired almost immediately. Kimmel returned to air less than a week later with stronger ratings than before, and his renewed jabs at Trump prompted the president to demand that ABC “get the bum off the air.”
Instead, Kimmel received a contract extension in December — a sharp reversal that underscored both his resilience and his continued relevance in the late‑night landscape.

The Oscars’ In Memoriam segment unfolded with an unusual sense of calm this year, allowing each name to land with real weight. Rather than rushing through the montage, the producers let the moment breathe, creating a pace closer to a memorial service than a standard awards‑show interlude.
Actors including Billy Crystal, Rachel McAdams, and Barbra Streisand stepped forward to offer brief, personal tributes, giving the segment a human texture that elevated it beyond a simple list of losses. “My friend Rob’s movies will last a lifetime, because they’re about what make us laugh and cry, and what we aspire to be,” Crystal said, his voice steady but unmistakably emotional.

It’s also far from the first time Penn has missed Hollywood’s biggest night. He previously no‑showed as a best actor nominee in 1996, 2002, and 2003, underscoring a long‑standing ambivalence toward the pageantry of awards season.
Penn has attended the Oscars only when absolutely necessary, including his best actor wins for “Mystic River” in 2004 and “Milk” in 2009. Ryan Coogler’s Sinners emerged as one of 2025’s most acclaimed films — a supernatural horror drama set in the Mississippi Delta in 1932, anchored by Michael B. The film blends period detail, genre tension, and social history, supported by a cast that includes Hailee Steinfeld, Miles Caton, Jack O’Connell, Wunmi Mosaku, Jayme Lawson, Omar Benson Miller, and Delroy Lindo.
Developed through Coogler’s Proximity Media and acquired by Warner Bros. after a competitive bidding war, Sinners was shot in 2024 and premiered the following spring. Composer Ludwig Göransson, a longtime Coogler collaborator, crafted the score and served as an executive producer, helping shape the film’s atmospheric world.
Upon its April 2025 release, Sinners became both a critical and commercial hit, earning more than $370 million worldwide and landing on year‑end top‑ten lists from the National Board of Review and the American Film Institute. Awards bodies responded in kind: the film received a record‑breaking 16 nominations at the 98th Academy Awards, along with major recognition from BAFTA, the NAACP Image Awards, the Critics’ Choice Awards, the Golden Globes, and the Actor Awards. Coogler ultimately won the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay.
The film’s success further solidified Coogler’s status as one of the most influential filmmakers of his generation. From Fruitvale Station to Black Panther and now Sinners, his work continues to shape contemporary cinema — and his latest achievement marks a new high point in an already remarkable career.

The message lands on Hollywood’s biggest stage — a night historically intertwined with political expression — and signals that concerns about press freedom will be part of the conversation long before the first award is handed out.

But for all the pressure and visibility, hosting the Oscars isn’t the lucrative job many assume it is.
Hosting the ceremony is a prestigious assignment, but it’s not a financial windfall. Past hosts have been candid about the economics: Wanda Sykes once revealed she was paid “scale,” the minimum rate for SAG‑AFTRA performers, and joked that the gig actually cost her money after factoring in prep time.
Jimmy Kimmel has said he earned $15,000 for hosting — a number that sounds generous until you consider the months of writing, rehearsing, and press that come with the job. He even turned down the 2025 ceremony because the workload pulled too much focus from his nightly show.
The Oscars are enormously expensive to produce, and the host fee is a tiny fraction of the overall budget. A decade‑old breakdown from The Hollywood Reporter estimated that the Academy spent more than $38 million on the show and its surrounding events — including tens of thousands of dollars on statuettes, envelopes, and honoraria. Even with inflation, the host’s paycheck remains one of the smallest line items.

98th Oscars by the numbers: Key stats behind Hollywood’s biggest night
The 98th Academy Awards arrive with a mountain of data that shows just how massive the ceremony has become. From record‑breaking eligibility totals to global reach, here’s a quick breakdown of the numbers shaping this year’s Oscars.
A total of 317 feature films qualified for Oscar consideration this year, with 202 of them eligible for best picture — one of the largest pools in modern Academy history. The international feature race also expanded, with 86 countries submitting films.
The Academy now includes 10,136 voting members, reflecting its continued growth and diversification. Behind the scenes, more than 700 crew members will work the live telecast, a reminder of the scale required to pull off Hollywood’s most-watched awards show.
Last year’s ceremony drew 19.7 million U.S. viewers and more than 21 million internationally. This year’s telecast will air in over 200 countries, underscoring the Oscars’ status as one of the world’s most widely viewed entertainment events.
The 98th Oscars will present 24 competitive categories, with the 97th ceremony handing out 45 statuettes. This year’s Governors Awards honored Debbie Allen, Tom Cruise and Wynn Thomas with honorary Oscars, while Dolly Parton received the Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award.
Since 1929, the Academy has awarded 3,491 competitive Oscars. Each statuette stands 13.5 inches tall, weighs 8.5 pounds, and features a knight holding a crusader’s sword atop a film reel with five spokes — representing the Academy’s original branches.
The longest Oscars broadcast ran 4 hours, 23 minutes in 2002; the shortest lasted 1 hour, 40 minutes in 1959. ABC has aired the show continuously since 1976 and will mark its 61st year as broadcaster.
The Dolby Theatre hosts the ceremony for the 23rd time, offering 3,300 seats and a red carpet stretching roughly 900 feet long and 33 feet wide. The venue trails only the Dorothy Chandler Pavilion, which has hosted 25 ceremonies.
Bob Hope remains the most frequent host with 19 appearances. The oldest poster in the Academy’s collection dates back to the 32nd Oscars in 1960. And the oversized set‑dressing Oscars seen onstage typically stand 7.5 feet tall and weigh 65 pounds.

Los Premios Oscar 2026 han servido para que la Academia de Hollywood salde su deuda con uno de los mejores directores las últimas décadas: Paul Thomas Anderson. El triunfo inapelable de Una batalla tras otra con seis estatuillas (mejor película, mejor dirección, mejor guion adaptado, mejor actor de reparto para Sean Penn, mejor montaje y mejor casting) supone su consagración dentro de la industria.
La segunda película con más triunfos ha sido Los pecadores,el fenómeno de Ryan Coogler. Su filme ha sumado cuatro muy importantes: mejor guion original para él, mejor actor protagonista para Michael B. Jordan en detrimento del pensado como favorito Timothée Chalamet, mejor música original para Ludwig Göransson y una histórica mejor fotografía para Autumn Durald Arkapaw, primera mujer premiada en la categoría.
La españolaSirat,de Oliver Laxe, no ha podido conseguir ninguno de los dos premios a los que aspiraba. El de mejor película internacional fue para la noruega Valor sentimental,que tuvo que conformarse con ese premio tras el inesperado triunfo sobre Stellan Skarsgard de un ausente Sean Penn.
Fue quizás lo más sorprendente de una noche en la que se cumplió lo esperado con Jessie Buckley coronándose como mejor actriz por Hamnet,o el triunfo de Las guerreras k-pop con los premios de mejor película de animación y mejor canción por Golden.
Autumn Durald Arkapaw ha ganado el premio por su trabajo en la película de Ryan Coogler, que suma su tercera estatuilla.
16/03/2026
'Una batalla tras otra', mejor montaje
Andy Jurgensen gana el premio por su trabajo en la película de Paul Thomas Anderson, que ya suma cuatro estatuillas.

El In Memoriam más emotivo

Gareth John, Al Nelson, Gwendolyn Yates Whittle, Gary A. Rizzo y Juan Peralta han ganado el premio al que también optaba 'Sirat'.
16/03/2026
'Los pecadores', mejor música original

'Mr. Nobody contra Putin', mejor película documental

'All the Empty Rooms', mejor corto documental

'Avatar: Fuego y ceniza', mejores efectos visuales
Joe Letteri, Richard Baneham, Eric Saindon y Daniel Barrett han ganado el premio, entregado también por Weaver y Pascal.

¿Qué le ha pasado a Pedro Pascal?

Tamara Deverell y Shane Vieau han ganado el premio, entregado por Sigourney Weaver y Pedro Pascal. Tercer galardón para la película de Guillermo del Toro.

Barbra Streisand recuerda a Robert Redford

In Memoriam extendido

sources.news_title: The Oscars 2026 live: One Battle After Another Wins Best Picture
sources.text:
One Battle After Another triumphed at the Academy Awards on Sunday night, winning six prizes including Best Picture.
The film, directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, also took home Best Director, Best Supporting Actor, Best Adapted Screenplay, Best Editing and Best Casting.
Accepting the award for Best Picture, Anderson was elated. “What a night, you guys. Let’s have a Martini, this is pretty amazing,” he said.
The director, whose films have earned 41 nominations but never before won Best Picture, said the winners depend on “what the mood might be that day”, before adding “we’re happy to be part of this wonderful, wonderful journey with our fellow nominees”.
Sean Penn, who won Best Supporting Actor for his role in the film, was not present to collect his award, skipping proceedings amid rumours that he had flown to Ukraine, according to The New York Times.
Jessie Buckley also won Best Actress for her performance in Hamnet.

sources.news_title: Check Out The Complete List Of 2026 Oscar Winners
sources.text:
The 98th Academy Awards kept film fans on the edge of their seats as two critically acclaimed thrillers vied for the most wins of the night.
Hosted by Conan O’Brien at Hollywood’s Dolby Theater on Sunday, the competition ended up being a dramatic back-and-forth between “Sinners” and “One Battle After Another.”
“Sinners” scooped up a record-shattering 16 nods, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Original Screenplay, when nominations were announced near the end of January.
But director Ryan Coogler’s supernatural-infused take on the Jim Crow South had Paul Thomas Anderson’s relentless political picture hot on its trail all awards season, as it scooped up best film at both the Golden Globes and BAFTA Awards, as well as at industry honors for the Directors and Producers guilds.
In the end, “One Battle” emerged as the victor, racking up six trophies, including Best Picture, Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Director, while “Sinners” earned four.
The vampire film’s leading man Michael B. Jordan did snag the Best Actor accolade for his double performance as the Smokestack twins, outshining “Marty Supreme’s” Timothée Chalamet, “One Battle” star Leonardo DiCaprio, Wagner Moura of Brazil’s “The Secret Agent” and Ethan Hawke of “Blue Moon.”
Best Actress went to “Hamnet’s” Jessie Buckley, whose win for the Shakespearean family tragedy seemed all but guaranteed after she practically swept the category during almost every other award ceremony this season. With her Oscar, she is now the first Irish person to win the top female lead.
Guillermo del Toro’s Gothic literary adaptation, “Frankenstein,” dominated the technical categories, with its creative teams collecting Best Costume Design, Best Makeup and Hairstyling and Best Production Design.
Other memorable moments included a tie in the Best Live-Action Short set, the very first Best Casting award and cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw making history as the first woman to win an Oscar for her craft.

sources.news_title: Meet the 2026 Oscar Nominees
Rare Oscars tie stuns winners: 'I didn't know that was a thing'
sources.text:
WASHINGTON — For just the seventh time in history, there was a tie at the Oscars.
While presenting the award for best live action short film on Sunday at the 98th Academy Awards, comedian Kumail Nanjiani announced there had been a tie.
"It's a tie, I'm not joking," Nanjiani revealed after opening the envelope on stage. "It's actually a tie, so everyone calm down we're going to get through this. Focus up"
It's such a rare feat that even the winners didn't know it was possible.
When "The Singers," the first of the two winners in the category came up, one of the winners remarked: "I didn't know that was a thing, a tie."
Before Nanjiani revealed the second winner, he remarked that it was ironic that the short film Oscar was going to take twice as long.
He then announced “Two People Exchanging Saliva” as the other winner.
"You just ruined 22 million Oscars pools," Academy Awards host Conan O'Brien joked after the category.
When has there been a tie at the Oscars?
Best actor in 1931/1932: Fredric March, Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde; Wallace Beery, The Champ. The Academy notes this wasn't a true tie as March had one more vote, but rules at the time said anything within three votes of the winner would be a "tie." The rules have since been changed, so only exact matches are a tie.
Best documentary in 1949: "A Chance to Live" and "So Much for So Little"
Best actress in 1968: Katharine Hepburn, "The Lion in Winter" and Barbra Streisand, "Funny Girl"
Best documentary in 1986: "Artie Shaw: Time Is All You've Got" and "Down and Out in America"
Best live action short film in 1994: "Franz Kafka's It's a Wonderful Life" and "Trevor"
Best sound editing in 2012: "Skyfall" and "Zero Dark Thirty"

Oscar 2026: Brasil disputa 5 prêmios com "O agente secreto"
Os preparativos para o Oscar 2026 estão a todo vapor, com o tapete vermelho no Dolby Theatre de Los Angeles prestes a receber estrelas como Michael B. Jordan e Emma Stone. O Brasil pode conquistar cinco prêmios com "O agente secreto". A cerimônia, apresentada por Conan O'Brien, será transmitida ao vivo às 21h deste domingo, em canais como TNT e HBO Max, além da Globo. Celebridades como Wagner Moura e Scarlett Johansson também participarão.
Na contagem regressiva para o Oscar 2026, que acontece neste domingo (15), o icônico tapete vermelho do tradicional Dolby Theatre, em Los Angeles, nos EUA já está em fase de preparação final. O GLOBO acompanha de perto a 98ª edição da premiação, que pode dar ao Brasil cinco estatuetas, com "O agente secreto", nas categorias de melhor filme, melhor filme internacional, melhor ator (Wagner Moura) e melhor casting (Gabriel Domingues) e com Adolpho Veloso, que concorre ao prêmio de direção de fotografia pelo filme "Sonhos de trem".
- Indicados ao Oscar 2026: veja lista completa e as chances de 'O Agente Secreto' na premiação

No vídeo exclusivo, a repórter especial Mariane Morisawa revela detalhes do tapete vermelho, que inclui uma área para fãs e para entrevistas. A partir das 18h30, celebridades como Michael B. Jordan, Timothée Chalamet, Emma Stone, Kate Hudson e Leonardo DiCaprio, indicados para os principais prêmios da noite, chegam ao local. Confira:
Preparativos do Oscar: Hollywood estende o tapete vermelho
A cerimônia reúne os principais nomes da indústria audiovisual e será transmitida ao vivo, a partir das 21h, para diversos países.
Horário do Oscar e onde assistir transmissão ao vivo
Na TV por assinatura e no streaming, a transmissão do prêmio fica a cargo da TNT e HBO Max, respectivamente, a partir das 18h30, com a cerimônia começando às 21h. Na TV aberta, a Globo passa a premiação ao vivo, depois do Fantástico, também com previsão de 21h. G1 e gshow retransmitem o sinal.
Quem apresenta o Oscar?
Assim como em 2025, o apresentador da cerimônia será Conan O'Brien. Nomes importantes de Hollywood já estão confirmados para subirem ao palco com a função de apresentarem prêmios ou cumprirem alguma função importante na festa. Selena Gomez, Oprah Winfrey, Jo Alwyn, Sterling K.Brown, William Dafoe, Ana de Armas, Lily Rose-Depp, Goldie Hawn, Connie Nielsen, Ben Stiller, Halle Berry, Pénelope Cruz, Elle Fanning, Whoopi Goldberg, Scarlett Johansson, John Lithgow, Amy Poehler, June Squibb e Bowen Yang são alguns dos artistas recrutados pela Academia.
A Academia também anunciou a presença do ator Wagner Moura como um dos apresentadores da noite.

sources.news_title: Oscars 2026 Live Updates: Barbra Streisand, Billy Crystal Mourn Robert Redford, Rob Reiner; Tie For Best Live Action Short Film
