Oscars 2026 Recap: ‘One Battle After Another’ Wins Best Picture; Michael B. Jordan, Jessie Buckley Win Best Actor, Actress
Here are all the highlights from the 98th Academy Awards on Sunday, March 15.
The Best Moments from the 2026 Oscars
- This year’s Academy Awards took place Sunday, March 15, starting at 7 p.m. ET and 4 p.m. PT. Both "Sinners" and "One Battle After Another" dominated the night after entering the ceremony with 16 and 13 nominations, respectively.
- "One Battle After Another" took home the marquee award of the night. Best picture was presented by Nicole Kidman and Ewan McGregor in a "Moulin Rouge" 25th anniversary reunion.
- Most of the nominees and winners attended the show — with the exception of Sean Penn, who won best supporting actor.
- Other notable presenters included Anne Hathaway and Anna Wintour; "Bridesmaids" stars Kristen Wiig, Maya Rudolph, Melissa McCarthy and Rose Byrne; father and son Bill and Lewis Pullman; previous winners Adrien Brody and Mikey Madison, and more.
- In an exceptionally emotional in memoriam segment, Billy Crystal spoke to the legacy of Rob Reiner, Rachel McAdams to Diane Keaton and Barbra Streisand to Robert Redford.
- Conan O'Brien hosted the Oscars for the second year in a row. He opened and closed the show with pre-recorded skits spoofing first "Weapons," then "One Battle After Another" — with plenty of zingers and digs directed at audience members in between.
- Here’s how to watch the best picture nominees.
Conan O'Brien Sends a Subtle Message to Martin Short
As the Oscars were closing, host Conan O'Brien ended his duties by sending a message to his friend, Martin Short.
“We love you Marty Short,” the comedian shouted before the final skit aired and the credits rolled.
The nod comes after Short's daughter, Katherine Short, died last month at the age of 42.
A rep for the Short family confirmed her death in a statement shared with TODAY.com on Tuesday, Feb. 24.
“It is with profound grief that we confirm the passing of Katherine Hartley Short. The Short family is devastated by this loss, and asks for privacy at this time,” the statement read. “Katherine was beloved by all and will be remembered for the light and joy she brought into the world.”
The Final Oscars Tallies Are...
The following films won multiple Oscars during the 2026 Oscars ceremony.
"One Battle After Another": 6
"Sinners": 4
"Frankenstein": 3
"KPop Demon Hunters": 2
'One Battle After Another' Wins Best Picture
The final award of the night has been handed to Paul Thomas Anderson for his film "One Battle After Another," the best picture winner.
Entering the night, "One Battle After Another" had 13 nominations. It ended the ceremony with six wins and Anderson on stage celebrating with stars Teyana Taylor, Chase Infiniti, Leonardo DiCaprio and Regina Hall.
Producer Sara Murphy gave the acceptance speech. "Getting to make this film with this cast and this crew, and Paul, has already been the greatest filmmaking experience I can fathom," she said. "So receiving this award is just beyond. My heart is exploding with gratitude."
She thanked her producing partners, family and Warner Bros. before Anderson took over.
He listed the best picture nominees in 1975, which included "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest" and "Jaws." "There is no best among them. There is just what that mood might be that day. But we're happy to be a part of this," he said.
He added that he "blew it" when he won his best directing award and didn't thank his cast. So, he made up for it by saying all their names.
"What a night. You guys, let's have a martini. This is pretty amazing. Cheers!" he concluded.
Oscars End with Conan O'Brien Spoofing Sean Penn's Fate in 'One Battle After Another'
Spoilers ahead for the newly minted best picture nominee "One Battle After Another."
The 2026 Oscars ended with another skit from host Conan O'Brien. This time, he spoofed the fate of Sean Penn's character in "One Battle After Another." After Penn's character, Lockjaw, went to great lengths to secure his place in the white supremacist organization, the Christmas Adventurers Club, his "reward" of a new office turns out to be a death sentence.
Similarly, in the final skit, O'Brien is told he'll be the Oscars "host for life," receiving a corner office in the process. But after propping his feet up on his new desk, green gas fills the room, and he's seen being wheeled out and put into a furnace.
The "host for life" name on the door is replaced with "Mr. Beast," referring to the YouTuber with nearly 30 million subscribers.
Jessie Buckley Wins Best Actress for 'Hamnet'
Jessie Buckley won her first Oscar for best actress in a leading role for her performance in the drama "Hamnet."
The movie is a fictional account of William Shakespeare and his wife, Agnes Hathaway, who are forced to cope with the loss of their 11-year-old son Hamnet.
Buckley was the frontrunner for the Oscar after already winning in her category at this year's Critics Choice, Golden Globes, BAFTA and Actor Awards.
The Irish actor and singer, 36, who welcomed her first child, a daughter, last year with husand Freddie Sorensen, told her fellow nominees — Rose Byrne, Kate Hudson, Renate Reinsve, Emma Stone — she wanted "to work with every single one of you."
Buckley also thanked her parents for "teaching us to dream" and joked to Sorenson that she wanted to have "20,000 more babies" with him.
It's a 'Moulin Rouge' Reunion!
Ewan McGregor and Nicole Kidman took the Oscars stage to celebrate 25 years since the film premiered in 2001.
Speaking about the value of "love," the two took a moment to croon some of their most memorable lyrics from "Elephant Love Medley."
Adrien Brody Pokes Fun at His Long Acceptance Speech From Last Year's Oscars
Last year leading actor Oscar winner Adrien Brody poked fun at himself when presenting the best actor category.
First Conan O'Brien joked about Brody's extra long 2025 acceptance speech, saying, “Our next presenter heroically saved last year’s Oscars from running short. Please welcome Oscar winner Adrien Brody.”The actor then walked on stage and took out pages and pages of notes as music started playing. He then cracked that he did have something very important to say, which was to present the nominees for best actor in a leading role.
Michael B. Jordan Wins Best Actor for 'Sinners'
The audience leapt to their feet and loudly applauded as Michael B. Jordan won the best actor Oscar for his flawless portrayal of twins Smoke and Stack in "Sinners."
After last year's recipient Adrien Brody poked fun at his lengthy speech, he presented the Oscar to Jordan, who appeared stunned when his name was read.
He celebrated with his co-stars and mom before taking the stage as the thunderous applause continued.
"Man, God is good," he began. "Mama, what's up? Y'all know how I feel about my mother."
He added that his father was also in attendance and flew in from Ghana to go to the ceremony. His brother and sister and other members of his family were there, too.
Jordan spoke about the importance of "betting on a culture and betting on original ideas and original artistry." He said he was "honored" to call director Ryan Coogler a collaborator and a friend.
"You gave me the opportunity and a space for me to be seen. I love you to death," he told Coogler before thanking the cast.
He recognized the Black actors who have accepted Oscars before him, including Sidney Poitier, Denzel Washington, Halle Berry, Jamie Foxx, Forest Whitaker and Will Smith.
"I know you guys want me to do well and I want to do that because you guys bet on me," he said about his supporters. "And I'm going to keep stepping up. I'm going to keep being the best version of myself I can be."
'KPop Demon Hunters' Wins for Original Song
“KPop Demon Hunters” continued to win at the Oscars when the movie’s global hit anthem “Golden” won in the best original song category.
The song is co-written by K-pop songwriter/producer EJAE and composer Mark Sonnenblick and performed by the movie's fictional group HUNTR/X. It is the first K-pop song to win an Oscar.
“KPop Demon Hunters” also won an Oscar for best animated feature earlier in the ceremony.
The award was presented by music legend Lionel Richie, who noted he won an Oscar for best original song 40 years ago for the ballad "Say You, Say Me" from the motion picture "White Nights."
Other songs nominated in the best original song category included “Dear Me” from “Diane Warren: Relentless," “Highest 2 Lowest” from “Highest 2 Lowes," “I Lied To You” from “Sinners," "Sweet Dreams of Joy” from “Viva Verdi!” and “Train Dreams” from “Train Dreams.”
Paul Thomas Anderson Wins Oscar for Best Director: 'You Make A Guy Work Hard for One of These '
Paul Thomas Anderson won the Oscar for best directing for "One Battle After Another," his first time winning the award after directing films like "Boogie Nights" and "There Will Be Blood."
“You make a guy work hard for one of these," he quipped in his speech.
He also shouted out his "classmates" and fellow nominees, including Chloé Zhao and Ryan Coogler.
While Anderson said he'll always doubt that he deserves the award, "there is no question at the pleasure of having it for myself."
In the audience, partner Maya Rudolph as well as "One Battle After Another" stars Teyana Taylor, Chase Infiniti and Leonardo DiCaprio cheered exuberantly.
'Sentimental Value' Wins Best International Feature Film
The cast of "Sentimental Value" all joined director Joachim Trier on stage as he accepted the Oscar for best international feature film.
After presenters Priyanka Chopra and Javier Bardem announced the list of nominees and revealed the Norwegian film as the winner, Trier reflected on his career.
"I'm just a film nerd from Norway," he said. "Thank you so much, honestly. This means the world to me."
"This film is about a very dysfunctional family and it's the opposite of what I felt with this beautiful group behind me. I think I make films to feel at home with people. I really felt at home with (the) crew. There's 1,072 people in these credits and I love them all and I share this with them," he added.
He also took a moment recognize his fellow nominees: “The Secret Agent,” “It Was Just an Accident,” “Sirat” and “The Voice of Hind Rajab.”
'Sinners' Wins Oscar for Cinematography, Marking 1st Woman to Receive the Award
"Sinners" cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw took home the Oscar for best cinematography.
She thanked director Ryan Coogler for trusting her vision for the film.
Arkapaw, who per the LA Times and Variety is the first woman to win this Oscar, also asked all the women in the room to stand up to be applauded, explaining that their contributions helped her to succeed.
"Moments like this happen because of you guys," she said.
The category was rounded out by “Frankenstein," “Marty Supreme," “One Battle After Another" and "Train Dreams.”
HUNTR/X From 'KPop Demon Hunters' Deliver 'Golden' Performance at Oscars
They're goin’ up, up, up, it was HUNTR/X's moment at the 2026 Oscars.
Ejae, Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami, better known as the singing voices behind the "KPop Demon Hunters” girl group, performed their hit and Oscar-nominated song “Golden.”
The performance was a celebration of the film, which won the best animated film Oscar earlier in the telecast, and included a fusion of traditional Korean instrumentalists and dance. Before the performance, the Academy noted that it would also honor “the folklore and cultural inspiration that anchors the story behind this animated blockbuster.”
Dancers filled the stage as voiceover from the film was heard and the animated film was shown in the back. HUNTR/X, dressed in all white, then kicked off their spectacular performance that got the crowd excited.
The singers showcased their incredible vocals as the audience held yellow light sticks.
"KPop Demon Hunters" premiered June 20, 2025, and follows dueling K-pop groups with secret supernatural origins. Months after its release, six songs from the movie’s soundtrack took over Billboard’s Hot 100 chart, with two rising into the top 10 slots, according to Billboard’s website.
The Best Picture Race Remains Tight
"One Battle After Another" and "Sinners" entered tonight's Oscars dominating the nominations, and with several categories still to go, there's seemingly no clear favorite.
The two heavyweight films are taking turns receiving big wins. "One Battle After Another" currently has four wins: best casting, best supporting actor, best adapted screenplay and best film editing.
"Sinners," meanwhile, has three: best original screenplay, best original score and best cinematography.
'One Battle After Another' Wins Oscar for Best Editing, Presented by Bill and Lewis Pullman
Father-son duo Bill and Lewis Pullman teamed up to present the Oscar for best film editing, where they worked in a few comments about the experience of working in the same industry as your relative.
The Oscar went to Andy Jurgensen for "One Battle After Another."
'F1' Wins Best Sound
Add "F1" to the list of winners this evening as the blockbuster picked up an Oscar for best sound.
To collect the golden statue, sound engineers Gareth John, Al Nelson, Gwendolyn Yates Whittle, Gary A. Rizzo and Juan Peralta took the stage.
Peralta thanked everyone who worked on the film for "supporting such a fun cinematic experience."
John and Whittle also expressed gratitude for their entire sound team and their families. Whittle ended her remarks by encouraging film lovers to go watch and support movies.
'Sinners' Wins Award for Original Score
"Sinners" composer Ludwig Göransson won the Oscar for best original score, which was presented with no shortage of quips by the reunited stars of "Bridesmaids."
It was a third Oscar win for the Swedish musician, who previously won in 2019 for "Black Panther" and in 2024 for "Oppenheimer."
Other movies nominated for original score included “Bugonia," “Frankenstein," “Hamnet” and “One Battle After Another.”
'Bridesmaids' Stars Bring the Laughter in Oscars Reunion
The stars of "Bridesmaids" were ready to party at the 2026 Oscars.
Kristen Wiig, Maya Rudolph, Melissa McCarthy, Rose Byrne and Ellie Kemper reunited on stage to present best original score and best sound. The ladies walked out to an instrumental version of “Hold On" by Wilson Phillips, the song they dance to at the end of the film.
During their time on stage, they did a bit where they read notes from the audience.
“Well mine says, ‘First of all, you ladies look extremely beautiful tonight... You’re all aging well, signed Stellan Skarsgård,’” Rudolph read.
Byrne was next, reading, "Rose, can you please stop looking at me? The eye contact is too much. I’m thinking of leaving. I’m very uncomfortable. Sincerely, Leonardo DiCaprio."
McCarthy also read a note that said, "I’m with Stellan Skarsgård writing my own separate note. I also agree you ladies look radiant. All the things you’ve done to your faces are very tasteful. Yours truly, Elle Fanning."
She then said there was more, reading, "Just kidding, it’s me, again, Stellan Skarsgård."
The notes continued before they wrapped up their bit and announced the nominees in the category.
The moment comes as the comedy, directed by Paul Feig, celebrates its 15th anniversary. The film earned two Oscar nominations: best performance by an actress in a supporting role for McCarthy and best original screenplay for Wiig and co-writer Annie Mumolo.
It's also a special night for Byrne, who is nominated for her first Academy Award for her role in “If I Had Legs I’d Kick You.”
'Mr. Nobody Against Putin' Wins Best Documentary Feature Film
Jimmy Kimmel, who previously hosted the Academy Awards four times, was also on site tonight to present the award for best documentary feature film to the team behind "Mr. Nobody Against Putin."
David Borenstein, Pavel Talankin, Helle Faber and Alžběta Karásková went on stage to accept the honor.
Borenstein said their film "was about how you lose your country." He continued, "What we saw when working with this footage is that you lose it through countless, small little acts of complicity. When we act complicit. When a government murders people on the streets of our major cities. When we don't say anything. When oligarchs take over the media and control how we can produce it and consume it."
As the crowd applauded, he concluded, "We all face a moral choice, but luckily even a nobody is more powerful than you think."
The star of the film, Talankin, then spoke via a translator. He said, "In the name of our future, in the name of all of our children, stop all of these wars now."
'All the Empty Rooms' Wins Best Documentary Short Film
Moving right along, Jimmy Kimmel took the stage to present the Oscar for the best documentary films.
After a quick jab at Conan O'Brien's hosting gig, claiming he's taking over the role going forward, Kimmel celebrated the filmmakers who risk their lives to create documentaries.
The winners of best documentary short film was Joshua Seftel and Conall Jones for "All the Empty Rooms," a film that shows the bedrooms of children killed in school shootings.
To accept the award, the mother of Jackie Cazares, who was killed in the Uvalde school shooting in May 2022, said she hopes if people see this film, "we'd be a different America."
'Avatar: Fire and Ash' Wins Visual Effects Oscar
James Cameron's "Avatar: Fire and Ash" joins the list of movies that earned an Oscar at this year's ceremony.
The third installment in the franchise won for best visual effects. Joe Letteri, Richard Baneham, Eric Saindon and Daniel Barrett accepted the honor.
During his acceptance speech, Baneham revealed that 2,200 artists worked on film. "This is a massive, massive collaboration on the visual effects side," he said as he also thanked all their families.
Saindon then recognized the late film producer Jon Landau, who died in July 2024 as Variety reported.
"We miss you and you're still the heart and soul of this movie," Saindon said.
'Frankenstein' Wins Production Design
“Frankenstein” continued to win big during the 2026 Oscars, winning the award for production design. Tamara Deverell and Shane Vieau took the stage to thank director Guillermo del Toro, everyone they worked with, as well as "Frankenstein" novelist Mary Shelley.
Others nominated in the category included “Hamnet,” “Marty Supreme," “One Battle After Another” and “Sinners.”
Why Isn't Sean Penn at the Oscars? (He Was a Winner!)
Sean Penn won the best supporting actor Oscar for his performance in "One Battle After Another" but the acting legend was nowhere to be found during the ceremony.
"Sean Penn couldn’t be here this evening, or didn’t want to, so I’ll be accepting the award of his behalf,” presenter Kieran Culkin quipped.
Penn skipped several high-profile awards events this season after showing up to the Golden Globes and losing to “Sentimental Value" star Stellan Skarsgård. Penn appeared in the audience throughout the ceremony conspicuously smoking cigarettes.
Penn then failed to show up to the Actor Awards and the BAFTAs in London. Turns out, he won in his category at both his events.
And tonight, he's an Oscar winner for the third time.
Penn previously won best actor Oscars for 2009’s “Milk” and 2004’s “Mystic River."
Penn has been nominated five times in all and opted to skip three of the ceremonies.
He previously told Variety in 2023 he would be willing to melt down his Oscar statues to make bullets for the Ukrainian war effort.
Barbra Streisand Sings 'The Way We Were' For Late Co-Star Robert Redford
To remember the late great Robert Redford, who died in September 2025, Barbra Streisand took the Oscars stage to share her favorite memories with the actor, including the story behind his nickname for her, "Babs."
She also took the mic to sing part of "The Way We Were," a song featured in their 1973 classic romance film of the same name.
Rachel McAdams Remembers Catherine O'Hara and Diane Keaton
In another set of tributes, Rachel McAdams took the stage to remember the lives of Catherine O'Hara and Diane Keaton.
McAdams called O'Hara her "fellow Canadian" and remembered her as an actor who made everyone laugh until they cried.
She then honored the legacy of Diane Keaton, whom McAdams worked with on "The Family Stone." She remembered Keaton's presence on set and her love for her family.
Billy Crystal and Meg Ryan Honor Rob Reiner in Emotional Tribute
"When Harry Met Sally..." co-stars Billy Crystal and Meg Ryan took the stage during the Academy Awards to pay tribute to the late Rob Reiner.
Crystal opened the in memoriam section of the show with a moving tribute to Reiner's work in Hollywood and his life of activism.
Rob Reiner, who directed the 1989 rom-com, and wife Michele Singer Reiner were found dead in their Los Angeles home on Dec. 14 from apparent stab wounds, a source told NBC News at the time.
Rob Reiner, who had a lengthy acting career starred in “All in the Family,” “The First Wives Club,” “New Girl,” and “The Bear.” He also directed “This Is Spinal Tap,” “A Few Good Men” “Stand By Me” and “The Princess Bride,” among others.
After his moving words, Crystal was joined by Ryan and other stars of Reiner's films, including Demi Moore, Kathy Bates, Mandy Patinkin and more.
Paul Thomas Anderson wins 1st Oscar for Adapted Screenplay
After 14 nominations, acclaimed director Paul Thomas Anderson can finally add an Oscar to his resume.
He kissed longtime partner Maya Rudolph before heading to the stage to collect his first golden statue.
After the audience gave him a standing ovation, Anderson said he was "incredibly honored to be a part of this history."
He thanked author Thomas Pynchon, who wrote the book "Vineland," which the film is inspired by.
"Any writer knows that you either beg for forgiveness or your special thanks is really to your family and the people that you share a roof with, who put up with what it means to live with a writer," he continued before naming Rudolph and their children.
Anderson added, "I wrote this movie for my kids to say sorry for the housekeeping mess that we left in this world we're handing off to them. But also with the encouragement that they will be the generation that hopefully brings up some common sense and decency."
'Sinners' Wins Best Original Screenplay, Marking Ryan Coogler's First Oscar
Ryan Coogler won the Academy Award for best original screenplay for the blockbuster hit "Sinners." To thunderous applause, Coogler thanked the Academy and his fellow nominees, as well as his family and his parents, who were in the crowd.
Coogler is up for two more awards tonight, and he has five nominations overall.
This is the first win of the night for "Sinners," which entered the ceremony with 16 nominations — the most ever in the history of the Oscars.
Robert Downey Jr. and Chris Evans Reunite 14 Years After 1st 'Avengers'
It's a mini "Avengers" reunion!
Robert Downey Jr. and Chris Evans reunited on the Oscars stage for a bit about their "anniversary."
"It's the 14th-year anniversary of our first 'Avengers' movie. I got you a signed copy of the original script, signed by the whole cast. It's backstage. See I really thought this through," Evans said.
In return, Downey playfully gave Evans his valet ticket before the two presented the award for best adapted screenplay.
When the two returned to present best original screenplay, Downehy had an upgraded gift: Channing Tatum's "Magic Mike" thong.
Tatum then chimed in from the audience and said he needed the underwear back because he had to work later.
Sean Penn Wins Best Supporting Actor Despite Missing Oscar Awards Ceremony
Sean Penn won an Oscar for best supporting actor for his role in "One Battle After Another," though the star wasn't in attendance.
Kieran Culkin, who presented the award, accepted it on Penn's behalf in his absence.
"Sean Penn couldn't be here this evening, or didn't want to, so I'll be accepting the award of his behalf," Culkin, who won best supporting actor in 2025, said.
Penn beat out co-star Benicio Del Toro, Jacob Elordi, Delroy Lindo and Stellan Skarsgard.
Two Movies Share Win for Live Action Short Film
It was a tie in the live action short film category.
The award went to two films: “The Singers” and “Two People Exchanging Saliva.”
“The Singers” is a short musical comedy directed by Sam A. Davis that features a cast sourced in part through viral videos.
The French-language “Two People Exchanging Saliva,” written and directed by Natalie Musteata and Alexandre Singh, “is a “weird” and “queer” film about the power of connection in a dystopian world that forbids kissing, Musteata said during her acceptance speech.
Other live action short films nominated in the same category included “Butcher’s Stain,” “A Friend of Dorothy” and “Jane Austen’s Period Drama.”
Conan O'Brien Leaves Note and Snacks for Attendees
Conan O'Brien may be hosting the Oscars, but he also left a note and "moderately happy meal" for nominees, plus ones and seat fillers inside the Dolby Theatre.
Shared by Deadline, the message begins with the comedian welcoming the guests to the awards show.
"These snacks may not look like much but in any movie theater they would run you $85," it read, reminding people to have fun and that laughter is "good for your health and ego."
It concluded with a drawing of O'Brien.
Cassandra Kulukundis Wins First-Ever Oscar for Casting
"One Battle After Another" casting director Cassandra Kulukundis made history at the 2026 Oscars as the first-ever recipient of an Academy Award for achievement in casting.
For the inaugural award, stars from each of the nominated films were tapped to deliver sweet remarks to their respective casting directors: "Hamnet" star Paul Mescal, "Marty Supreme" star Gwyneth Paltrow, "One Battle After Another" star Chase Infiniti, "The Secret Agent" star Wagner Moura and "Sinners" star Delroy Lindo.
The new category was the first addition to the ceremony in 24 years, the broadcast said.
While accepting the distinct honor, Kulukundis thanked the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and her fellow casting directors for the category being recognized "despite everything in their way."
She added, "I dedicate this to you" and to the casting directors who didn't get their credit in the past.
Speaking directly to director Paul Thomas Anderson, she said, "I just thank you, I mean, for 10 movies. We've done this for over 30 years. We grew up together, I guess, and this is freaking insane. And I had one before you which is also crazy. I hope you get one tonight."
'Frankenstein' Wins for Makeup and Hairstyling
The hair and makeup team behind Guillermo del Toro’s “Frankenstein” won the Oscar in the makeup and hairstyling category.
Led by Mike Hill, Jordan Samuel and Cliona Furey, the team created a fresh look for the monster protagonist of Mary Shelley's classic work of gothic literature, played in the film by Jacob Elordi.
Other films nominated in the same category included “Kokuho,” “Sinners,” “The Smashing Machine” and “The Ugly Stepsister”
'Frankenstein' Wins Best Costume Design
After an iconic presentation by Anne Hathaway and Anna Wintour, the Oscar for best costume design went to "Frankenstein," which beat out “Avatar: Fire and Ash," “Hamnet," “Marty Supreme” and “Sinners."
Guillermo Del Toro's "Frankenstein" is a moody, Gothic film adaptation of Mary Shelley's classic novel. For the film, Jacob Elordi became unrecognizable as the titular character's monster.
Anna Wintour Takes a 'Devil Wears Prada' Dig at Anne Hathaway While Presenting: 'Thank You, Emily'
Ahead of the release of "Devil Wears Prada 2" in April, Anne Hathaway stepped out on the Oscars stage alongside the film franchise's long rumored inspiration, Anna Wintour.
For the sketch, Hathaway asked Wintour for her thoughts on her Oscars outfit. Donning her signature black sunglasses and giving nothing away, Wintour simply responded, "And the nominees are..."
The two also presented the best makeup and hairstyling category, with Hathaway leading the way.
As she ended, Wintour simply quipped, "Thank you, Emily," before announcing the nominees.
Timothée Chalamet and Kylie Jenner Have a Date Night at the Oscars
Timothée Chalamet and Kylie Jenner made their way inside the Dolby Theatre looking like superstars.
The beauty entrepreneur wore a red sequin gown to support her boyfriend, the "Marty Supreme" star who is nominated for best actor. The two were hand-in-hand as they made their way to their seats.
Miles Caton and Raphael Saadiq Bring 'Sinners' to the Stage
“Sinners” was celebrated at the 2026 Oscars when Miles Caton and Raphael Saadiq performed the Academy Award-nominated original song “I Lied To You” from the film.
Bringing Ryan Coogler's creation to life, the whole stage was filled with dancers and musicians that included Misty Copeland, Eric Gales, Buddy Guy, Brittany Howard, Christone “Kingfish” Ingram, Jayme Lawson, Li Jun Li, Bobby Rush, Shaboozey and Alice Smith.
The performance was “an homage to the film’s singular visual style,” the Academy said prior to the show — and it truly was just that!
As they ended the dynamic track, they got a standing ovation from the audience.
'KPop Demon Hunters' Wins Best Animated Feature
The Oscar for best animated feature went to “KPop Demon Hunters.”
The animated blockbuster debuted on Netflix in June 2025 and has racked up more than 500 million views, according to the streaming service. (A sequel is also in the works.)
Directed by Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans, “KPop Demon Hunters" tells the story of girl pop group HUNTR/X that battles demons when they're not thrilling fans onstage.
The movie features a voice ensemble that includes Arden Cho, May Hong, Ji-young Yoo, Ahn Hyo-seop, Yunjin Kim, Joel Kim Booster, Liza Koshy, Daniel Dae Kim, Ken Jeong, and Byung Hun Lee.
The movie's soundtrack, which features singers EJAE, Audrey Nuna, Rei Ami, Andrew Choi, Danny Chung, Kevin Woo, samUIL Lee, Neckwav, and Lea Salonga, has scored multiple hit songs and even a Grammy win.
Other nominees in the animated film category included "Arco," "Elio," "Little Amélie or the Character of Rain" and “Zootopia 2."
'The Girl Who Cried Pearls' Wins Best Animated Short Film
Presenters Will Arnett and Channing Tatum announced "The Girl Who Cried Pearls" as the winner for best animated short film.
Co-directors Chris Lavis and Maciek Szczerbowski accepted the Oscar.
"People think it takes patience to take five years to make a puppet film. It actually takes patience to live with someone who takes five years to make a puppet film," Lavis said before thanking his wife and his daughter.
Szczerbowski then thanked his family, as well as the film's producers. He also expressed gratitude for their community and "the fantastic city of Montreal."
"Thank you, Canada!" the directors said in unison.
Amy Madigan Wins Best Actress in a Supporting Role
Amy Madigan is officially the first winner of the night, taking home the Oscar for best actress in a supporting role!
Last year's winner, Zoe Saldaña returned to the Oscar's stage to hand out the award to the "Weapons" star.
The 75-year-old actor, who was previously nominated in 1986 for "Twice in a Lifetime," seemed to be in disbelief and began laughing, just like her character's signature cackle, as she started her speech.
"This is great," she said. "Everybody's asking me in the press and all this, 'Well, it's been 40 years. What's different about this time?' What's different is I got this little gold guy!"
She then listed all the people who helped make this career milestone come true. She also thanked her fellow nominees, her daughter, her son-in-law and "all the dogs."
"Most important is my beloved, Ed (Harris), who's been with me forever," she added of her husband since 1983. "And that's a long ass time. None of this wouldn't mean anything if he wasn't by my side."
Conan O'Brien Creates a New DiCaprio Meme, Is Serenaded by Josh Groban in Oscars Monologue
Taking the stage for his second consecutive year hosting the Oscars, Conan O'Brien opened the ceremony with an uproarious monologue touching on a slew of topics.
First he starred in a skit spoofing his hair and makeup process, re-creating best supporting actress nominee Amy Madigan's look from "Weapons." As he's chased by children, he pops up in major scenes from some of this year's most notable films, including "Marty Supreme," "F1" and "Hamnet." (He even got the anime treatment for a brief cameo in "KPop Demon Hunters.")
When he formally started the monologue, he commented on current events and artificial intelligence, calling himself the "last human host" of the Oscars.
He also took a dig at Timothée Chalamet's viral comments about the opera and ballet, which the "Marty Supreme" star took in stride, laughing and wearing a wide grin in the audience beside girlfriend Kylie Jenner.
O'Brien also called out his own role in the Oscar-nominated film "If I Had Legs I'd Kick You." He celebrated his co-star Rose Byrne, who's up for best actress, and praised her ability to act opposite someone she had a crush on.
But what really got the audience cheering was O'Brien's note on best documentary shorts, calling it a category that may get less attention. The audience proved him wrong with uproarious applause even before his punchline, when he gave the films the nickname, "little sads."
He also called out best actor nominee Leonardo DiCaprio's history of meme-able moments and in the process, created a brand new one, captioning his shrugging expression at the camera, "TFW you didn't agree to this."
And for his grand finale, O'Brien re-created what he'd do if he was fortunate enough to win an Oscar. Donning a red robe and crown, Josh Groban made a cameo to serenade O'Brien's win before an eagle dropped the award into his hands.
Kate Hudson Brings Mom Goldie Hawn As Good-Luck Charm
Kate Hudson brought along her Oscar-winning mom Goldie Hawn as a good-luck charm to the 2026 Oscars.
Hudson wore a custom mint green Armani Privé gown she paired with Garatti jewelry. Hawn stunned in a sleek black dress with embellishments.
Hudson is nominated for best actress in a leading role for her performance opposite Hugh Jackman in the "Song Sung Blue," which tells the story of Mike and Claire Sardina, a real-life Milwaukee couple who performed together in a Neil Diamond tribute act.
The nomination marks the second time Hudson has entered the Oscar race. She was first nominated in 2001 for her role as music groupie Penny Lane in “Almost Famous.”
Hawn won an Oscar in the best supporting actress category for her performance opposite Walter Matthau in the 1969 comedy “Cactus Flower.” She was later nominated a second time for the 1980 comedy “Private Benjamin.”

Director Chloé Zhao is having a gothic moment on the red carpet.
The "Hamnet" director arrived in a head-to-toe black outfit, complete with a black veil that made the look. Her gown also featured oversized sleeves and a multi-tiered design at the bottom.
'KPop Demon Hunters' Stars Are Dressed to Impress
The voice stars of "KPop Demon Hunters" naturally slayed on the red carpet. The Oscar-nominated Netflix movie, which tells the story of a girl group whose members battle demons offstage, has reached more than 500 million views since its June 2025 debut.
The film's hit song, "Golden," is also nominated for best original song. HUNTR/X singers EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami will also perform the track during the ceremony.

Making its debut at the 2026 Oscars is the achievement in casting category.

This marks the first time a new category has been added since 2001, when the Academy added best animated feature.
According to Variety, the best casting category will be presented by a group they have dubbed “the Fab Five,” who “have distinct personal connections to the nominated casting directors, each illuminating a different artisan and what, exactly, the job entails.”
Showrunner Raj Kapoor told the trade that they “really needed to tell a story” with the presenters, adding, “Casting is so multifaceted and complex. We need to make people understand the importance of casting directors’ contributions to film.”

"KPop Demon Hunters" star Arden Cho had all eyes on her with a red carpet look by Korean designer Miss Sohee.
Cho wore a black metallic fishtail gown featuring lace details that she paired with a dramatic olive green wisteria-embellished shawl. The look came from the Miss Sohee Spring/Summer 2026 Couture Collection.
The design was "inspired by the founder’s Korean heritage and her penchant for antiques and old natural objects, reflected in the shapes and silhouettes of her collections," the label announced in a press release.
Arden spoke about her look while chatting with E! on the red carpet during an interview with "KPop Demon Hunters" co-star Ken Jeong.
"I feel incredible. I feel like a queen," she said, adding that she was channeling Rumi's "main character energy" from the film.
"(Miss Sohee's) also a Korean designer so I felt like it gave a little, nice nod to our movie and this special moment that we're having," she continued. "It's all hand embroidered."
'Heated Rivalry' Star Hudson Williams Makes His Oscars Debut
"Heated Rivalry" actor Hudson Williams, who has become one of Hollywood's biggest rising stars over the past few months, is attending his first Oscars.
The 25-year-old Canadian star was one of the first actors to walk the red carpet at the 2026 Oscars. He wore a classic black Balenciaga tuxedo for his debut that he accessorized with Bvlgari jewelry.
Williams explained to E!'s Zuri Hall how surreal it was to be asked to attend the event.
"The fact I'm invited to the Oscars is pretty crazy," he shared.
He also teased that he has exciting plans in the works.
"I'm like, 'What?' They want to work with me?' We're cooking," he said, without revealing too much.
Season 2 of "Heated Rivalry" is expected to start filming this summer.
Astrologers Predict Who Will Win at the 2026 Oscars

Overall Prediction: Jessie Buckley

2026 Oscars By the Numbers
As we wait for the ceremony to begin, let's run through some fun facts about the 2026 Oscars!
- The custom 25,000-square-foot carpet, which host Conan O'Brien helped roll out last week, is 900 feet long and 60 feet wide.
- There will be over 300 lights illuminating the stars on the red carpet.
- Over 400 people helped put the elaborate set inside the Dolby Theatre together.
- The creative team behind the 98th Academy Awards started planning the event about a year ago.
- The set was built about three weeks before Sunday, March 15.
- 2000 mini chocolate Oscars will be on hand to snack on during the show.
Where to Watch All the Best Picture Nominees at the 2026 Oscars
Typically, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences saves its most prestigious award for the end of the night: best picture.
This year, the category is stacked with a wide range of films that could all take the top prize. Among the list of nominees are Ryan Coogler’s “Sinners,” which scored a historic 16 nominations, Paul Thomas Anderson’s “One Battle After Another” and “Bugonia,” which marks director Yorgos Lanthimos and star Emma Stone’s fourth collaboration.
See all 10 nominees below, and find out where you can check them out.

Find out where you can watch all the Oscar-nominated films this year, here.
Who's Up for the Most Awards Tonight?
That title goes resoundingly to Ryan Coogler's "Sinners," which received a whooping 16 Oscar nominations — the most ever in the history of the Academy Awards.
The previous record for most nominations was 14 and held by “All About Eve” (1950), “Titanic” (1997) and “La La Land” (2016).
"One Battle After Another" also dominated the nominations field, receiving 13. Next up were fellow best picture nominees "Frankenstein," "Sentimental Value" and "Marty Supreme," which each received nine nods. "Hamnet" received eight.
Who's Performing at the 2026 Oscars?
There will be two performances this year during the 2026 Academy Awards telecast.
Ejae, Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami, better known as the singing voices behind HUNTR/X, will perform their hit and Oscar-nominated song “Golden” from “KPop Demon Hunters.”
Viewers can expect “a fusion of traditional Korean instrumentalists and dance, celebrating the folklore and cultural inspiration that anchors the story behind this animated blockbuster,” according to the Academy.
Additionally, Miles Caton and Raphael Saadiq will perform the Oscar-nominated original song “I Lied To You” from “Sinners.”
The duo will be joined by Misty Copeland, Eric Gales, Buddy Guy, Brittany Howard, Christone “Kingfish” Ingram, Jayme Lawson, Li Jun Li, Bobby Rush, Shaboozey and Alice Smith in what is described as “an homage to the film’s singular visual style.”

Who Is Hosting the 2026 Oscars?
For the 98th Academy Awards, comedian Conan O'Brien will return to host the ceremony after emceeing the event last year.
O'Brien's first run was so successful that The Hollywood Reporter announced he would host again about two weeks after the ceremony ended last year.
Ahead of taking on the challenge of overseeing the 2026 Oscars, O'Brien stopped by "Jimmy Kimmel Live!" to talk about his preparation.
"I've been working on this for a while. I've been out workshopping jokes at different clubs," he shared.
He added, "I love showing up where no one expects me to be there. They don't particularly want me to be there. It's really fun just to pop up and do it."
O'Brien said he learned that it will be difficult for him to make fun of "Train Dreams," a best picture nominee. He was also hoping something unexpected would happen to surprise fans at home, the audience and himself.
He then spoke about starring in the Oscar-nominated film "If I Had Legs I'd Kick You," joking that he was snubbed in the best supporting actor category. "I'm better than all of them combined. And yet, I was denied! Denied!" he playfully shouted.
How to Watch the 2026 Oscars
We are just hours away from some of Hollywood's biggest movie stars making their way to the Dolby Theatre to attend the 98th Academy Awards!
But before they take their seats inside, the actors, directors, costume designers and more creatives who worked on the Oscar-nominated films will pose on the red carpet.
Want to make sure you don't miss any of the major arrivals? ABC will air its 90-minute red carpet special, “On The Red Carpet at the Oscars: Countdown to Oscars,” starting at 3:30 p.m. ET/ 12:30 p.m. PT. That special will be followed by “On the Red Carpet at the Oscars” at 5 p.m. ET/ 2 p.m. PT and “The Oscars Red Carpet Show” beginning at 6:30 p.m. ET and 3:30 p.m. PT. Fans can also stream the ABC walk-up specials on OnTheRedCarpet.com and via the On the Red Carpet Facebook and YouTube pages.
E! will air a red carpet special as well, kicking off at 4 p.m. ET/ 1 p.m. PT.
Then, the 2026 Oscars will officially begin at 7 p.m. ET/ 4 p.m. PT. The awards ceremony will air on ABC and simultaneously stream on ABC.com and Hulu.

The biggest night in Hollywood is here, and we're following it all live.
The 2026 Oscars have officially arrived, bringing the film industry's awards season marathon to its glittering finale. After months of campaigns, red carpets, heated debates, and a seemingly endless stream of precursor awards, the winners of the 97th Academy Awards will finally be revealed tonight.
As always, the Oscars promise a little bit of everything: emotional speeches, surprise wins, viral moments, and at least one bit that will immediately become a meme. The ceremony is Hollywood's most visible celebration of filmmaking, but it's also become something of a real-time internet event, where reactions unfold just as quickly on social media as they do inside the Dolby Theatre.
Throughout the night, we'll be tracking the biggest developments as they happen. Ryan Coogler's film will face off against Paul Thomas Anderson's One Battle After Another in the race for Best Picture, setting up one of the night's most closely watched showdowns.

The 2026 Oscars red carpet is about the be a fashion extravaganza, and we can’t wait to see what nominees like Teyana Taylor, Jessie Buckley, and Timothée Chalamet will wear.
This year, these stars will be hoping to pick up awards and land a spot on best-dressed lists, but only time will tell if they’ll manage to be on par with some of the greatest Oscars fashion moments of all time. Yes, it can be hard to rival Halle Berry’s divine Elie Saab gown that she wore while winning the Best Actress award at the 2002 Oscars, but we’re hoping someone gives it a shot!
“I just remember feeling really great in this dress,” Berry told Vogue in 2022 of her iconic fashion moment. “The top was very open and free and just had these little flowers that sort of covered all the right bits that it needed to cover but the bottom was very regal and very grand.”
“I remember this was Elie Saab, but he wasn’t the Elie Saab we know now,” she continued. “He was a young designer who was just starting and at the time it wasn’t the biggest name I could’ve worn but there was something about this dress that made me feel uniquely myself.”
To take a look at Berry’s iconic dress and other looks that are cemented into Academy Award history, scroll below!
The Best-Dressed Oscar Moments Over the Years:
Click here to see more of our Oscars coverage, including how to watch for free, dramatic moments, and more.
-
Mikey Madison (2025)
At last year’s Oscars, Mikey Madison won the Best Actress award for her role in Anora in a piece of fashion history. The Dior gown was a custom recreation of a dress from a 1956 collection.
-
Gwyneth Paltrow (1999)
Gwyneth Paltrow’s iconic baby pink dress by Ralph Lauren will always go down in Oscars fashion history. She won that night for her role in Shakespeare in Love.
-
Ariana Grande (2025)
Ariana Grande’s Schiaparelli couture look was on the most dramatic and jaw-dropping looks to hit the carpet in 2025.
-
Julia Roberts (2001)
Another Best Actress winner dress as Julia Roberts in 2001 in this black and white Valentino dress. She won that night for her role in Erin Brockovich.
-
Cher (1988)
In one of our favorite Best Actress winners’ looks to date, Cher’s daring sheer Bob Mackie look in 1988 was truly sensational. She won her first Oscar that year for Moonstruck.
-
Carey Mulligan (2024)
Carey Mulligan was the Oscars’ best dressed in 2024 in this stunning trumped-style Balenciaga gown inspired by a 1951 vintage gown. The dress was perfectly accessorized with black matching gloves and emerald earrings.
-
Geena Davis (1990)
While Denzel Washington is the one with the Oscar in this picture, we can’t help but stare at Geena Davis and this stunning red gown she wore to the 1990 Oscars. What a standout!
-
Angela Bassett (2023)
Angela Bassett took our breath away in 2023 in this bright purple Moschina dress that perfectly hugged her curves. She styled the look with this statement Bulgari necklace.
-
Grace Kelly (1954)
Late Old Hollywood star Grace Kelly was known for her beauty and elegance. So, of course, it’s no surprise to see her on this list. She looked gorgeous in 1954 in this sea green dress at the Oscars designed by Edith Head. That night, she won a Best Actress statuette for The Country Girl.
-
Kate Hudson (2014)
Kate Hudson wore one of the most timeless gowns in this list in 2014 in this white Atelier Versace gown with a deep plunge, an open back and a cape detail on the sleeves.
-
Nicole Kidman (2018)
Nicole Kidman absolutely commanded the carpet in 2018 in this cobalt blue Armani Privé gown. One of our favorite looks of hers to date!
-
Michelle Williams (2006)
Michelle Williams brought some color to 2006 Oscars in this canary yellow Vera Wang dress. The red lips were the perfect styling choice!
-
Farrah Fawcett (1978)
While many of us didn’t grow up with Farrah Fawcett’s beauty gracing our screens, one good look at her in this golden gown at the 1978 Oscars shows just how much of a bombshell she was.
-
Gwyneth Paltrow (2012)
Gwyneth Paltrow looked like the epitome of elegance in the 2012 Oscars in this white Tom Ford gown with an attached cape.
-
Lupita Nyong’o (2014)
When Lupita Nyong’o won the Best Performance by an Actress in a Supporting Role Oscar in 2014 for 12 Years a Slave, she looked like a princess on stage in this baby Prada gown. A true Cinderella moment!
-
Nicole Kidman (2007)
Nicole Kidman showed the power of a red dress at the 2007 Oscars in this red Balenciaga halter gown with an oversized bow on the collar.
-
Halle Berry (2002)
It doesn’t get more iconic than this. Halle Berry absolutely wowed in 2002 when she wore this Elie Saab dress with a copper skirt and a sheer floral top. Berry won her first Best Actress Oscar that year for Monter’s Ball.
-
Charlize Theron (2004)
Another Oscar-winning look was Charlize Theron’s glittering Gucci gown in 2004. After baring it all for her role in Monster, seeing Theron look this incredible on the carpet was beyond impressive. She won her first Best Actress Oscar this year.
-
Angelina Jolie (2004)
Angelina Jolie commanded the 2004 Oscars red carpet in this ivory plunging dress by Marc Bouwer.
Actress Sydney Sweeney paid homage to the look at the 2024 Oscars Vanity Fair After-Party.
-
Cher (1998)
Cher is and will always be a fashion icon. In 1998, she left fans speechless in this beaded Bob Mackie gown.
-
Elizabeth Taylor (1970)
Hollywood icon Elizabeth Taylor showed off her hourglass silhouette at the 1970 Oscars in this sculpted lavender gown. The dress was designed by Edith Hed.
-
Cate Blanchett (2016)
Cate Blanchett looked so beautiful at the 2016 Oscars in this aqua Armani Privé gown with floral appliqués. The dress perfectly completed her blonde locks.
-
Hilary Swank (2005)
Hilary Swank pushed the envelope at the 2005 Oscars red carpet in this navy Guy Laroche dress with a daring open back. She won this year for her role in Million Dollar Baby.
-
Grace Kelly (1956)
Grace Kelly wowed once again in 1956 in this floral ballgown with a silk fabric across her chest.
-
Lauren Hutton (1975)
What we love about Lauren Hutton’s gown at the 1975 Oscars is how colorful it is. The pink, orange, white, and green come together beautifully in this timeless Halston dress.
-
Jamie Lee Curtis (1983)
Jamie Lee Curtis still wows on the carpet to this day, but this shimmering white dress she wore to the 1983 Oscars might still be one of our favorites.
-
Kate Winslet (1996)
Kate Winslet looked so sweet and bubbly at the 1996 Oscars in this Vivienne Westwood gown. If you ask us, we could see Ariana Grande rocking this look for the Wicked press tour any day now.
-
Zendaya (2022)
Zendaya went outside the box at the 2022 Oscars in this Valentino Couture cropped button down with a sequined silver skirt. The perfect mix of edgy but still fitting to the occasion!
-
Jennifer Lawrence (2011)
Before Jennifer Lawrence made her mark in Hollywood with movies like The Hunger Games and Silver Linings Playbook, Lawrence topped best dressed lists in 2011 in this Calvin Klein Collection simple yet classic red dress.
-
Anne Hathaway (2009)
Anne Hathaway has rocked quite a few gorgeous Oscars looks over the years but this sequined Armani Privé gown in 2009 might be our favorite.
-
Angelina Jolie (2012)
Who could ever forget Angelina Jolie’s leg moment? At the 2012 Oscars, the actress showed off her legs in a major way in this black Versace gown with a thigh-high slit.
-
Mila Kunis (2011)
Mila Kunis’s 2011 lavender Elie Saab dress, which contained lace and sheer all around, is one of fans’ favorite Oscars dresses to date.

This Is What the Oscars Really Are Like – You Should Resort to a Special Trick on the Red Carpet
sources.text:
Tie Los Angelesin arvostetuimmalle muutamalle sadalle metrille, Oscar-gaalan punaiselle matolle, aukeaa tarkan turvakontrollin jälkeen. Vielä siinäkin erotetaan jyvät akanoista, ja vain kaikkein tärkeimmät pääsevät astelemaan maailman medioiden salamavalojen edessä. Muut kävelevät kulisseissa kohti Dolby-elokuvateatteria, jossa Oscarit on pidetty vuodesta 2002 asti.
Mutta miten Ovation-ostoskeskuksen uumenissa olevaan viisikerroksiseen teatteriin pääsee? Yleensä musta vuokra-auto tuo tähdet oikeaan paikkaan, pysähdyspaikalle hieman ennen turvatarkastusta.
Eri sovellusten kautta tilatut kyydit saattavat jättää asiakkaansa jopa puolen kilometrin päähän sisäänkäynnistä, ja kuuluisan Hollywood ja Highland -risteyksen lähellä näkee iltapukuihin pukeutuneita vieraita kävelemässä kohti gaalakauden päätösjuhlaa.
Kutsuvieraita kehotetaan olemaan paikalla ainakin paria tuntia ennen seremonian alkua. Tosin kirkkaimmat tähdet saapuvat viimeisen tunnin tai puolen tunnin aikana. Tänä vuonna heihin kuuluvat muiden muassa Timothée Chalamet, Michael B. Jordan, Leonardo DiCaprio, Benicio del Toro, Sean Penn, Jacob Elordi, Emma Stone, Kate Hudson ja Jessie Buckley.
Pohjoismaista osaamista voi jännittää suoraan tai välillisesti ainakin 25 kategoriassa, kuten norjalaisen Sentimental Value -elokuvan näyttelijöiden ja elokuvantekijätiimin puolesta. Tai suomalaisfirman IPR.VC:n osarahoittaman tarinan isosta unelmasta eli Marty Supremen menestystä yhdeksässä eri kategoriassa. Timo Argillander ja Tanu-Matti Tuominen ovat sen vastaavia tuottajia.
Millaista itse gaalassa on? Tuottaja Tina Jøhnk Christensen, joka osallistui tilaisuuteen viime vuonna The Girl with the Needle -draaman tanskalaisdelegaation kanssa, kuvailee sitä seuraavasti.
– Olen käynyt useissa Hollywood-gaaloissa, mutta Oscareita ei voi verrata muihin. Esimerkiksi Golden Globes on pienempi, intiimimpi ja hauskempi. Oscarit ovat arvokkaammat ja vakavammat elokuva-alan juhlat, Jøhnk Christensen kertoo.
– Siellä ei ole samanlaista juhlameininkiä, mutta on silti taianomaista olla kaikkien elokuvatähtien ympäröimänä. Kutsu tuntui hyvin erityiseltä.
Punaisen maton veteraanilla on oma taktiikkansa. Jotta tunnelmasta pääsee nauttimaan, pitää kulkea rauhallisesti ja vältellä ainakin suurempien yhdysvaltalaismedioiden kameroita. Niille on usein omat isot tukikohtansa. Pienemmät mediat ovat yleensä maton toisella puolella. Kun turvamiehet hätistävät eteenpäin, kannattaa heitä kuunnella muutaman metrin verran.
– Punaisella matolla on mahdollista tervehtiä tuttuja tähtiä ja pr-ihmisiä ja puhua lyhyesti heidän kanssaan, Jøhnk Christensen kertoo.
Tie itse teatteriin vie massiivisen portaikon kautta, jonka päässä on yli 3300-paikkainen teatteri. Ensimmäisen kerroksen aulassa ja baarissa on mahdollista nähdä eniten ehdokkaita ja muita A-luokan tähtiä, kuten tämän vuoden palkintojen jakajia Javier Bardem, Demi Moore, Chris Evans, Adrien Brody ja Zoe Saldaña.
Myös tuon kerroksen vessoissa voi törmätä tuttuihin kasvoihin. Siksi tuloaulassa hengailee enemmän kutsuvieraita kuin muiden kerrosten baareissa.
Juuri ennen gaalan alkua ehdokkaat istuvat elokuvateatterin ensimmäisille penkkiriveille ja ovat sen juontaja Conan O’Brienin vitsien kohteena. Salin perällä ja muissa kerroksissa istuvat vähemmän tunnetut vieraat. Ohjelma venyy yleensä yli kolmen tunnin. Siksi ainakin ylempien kerrosten penkeillä on huikopalaa: boksi, jossa on pientä purtavaa ja vesipullo.
Mainostauoilla pääsee santsaamaan baariin tai käymään vessassa, ja eri kerrosten aulojen välillä voi kulkea. Lähetyksen aikana teatterin ovet pysyvät kiinni, mutta silloin tilaisuutta voi seurata aulojen televisiosta. Tyhjällä tähden paikalla on penkkinäyttelijä. Aiempina vuosina kuka tahansa pystyi hakemaan paikantäyttäjäksi, mutta nyt pestiin valitaan vain Oscar-akatemian jäseniä.
Kun ohjelmanumero on ohi ja parhaat palkittu, noin puolet juhlavieraista jatkaa Oscareiden virallisille Governor’s Ball -jatkoille. Toiset isot jatkot ovat Vanity Fair -lehden juhla, johon pääsee myös muita silmäätekeviä kuin itse gaalaan osallistuneet.
Sen lisäksi kaupunki on täynnä pienempiä elokuvayhtiöiden, tuotantofirmojen, agentuurien ja manageritoimistojen bileitä. Yhteistä niille on se, että jossain vaiheessa iltaa naiset vaihtavat korkokengät ballerinoihin – nykyään useimmat juhlat jakavat tossuja vierailleen.
Oscar-gaala Teema & Fem klo 0.30 su–ma yönä 15.–16.3.

sources.news_title: Oscars 2026: Polymarket Outlines "One Battle After Another" as the Undisputed Winner of the Ceremony
sources.text:
Oscars 2026: Polymarket perfila a “One Battle After Another”como la vencedora indiscutible de la ceremonia
La ceremonia de este domingo será presentada por Conan O’Brien. Los espectadores la podrán ver por ABC y Hulu
La 98ª edición de los Premios Oscar ya está aquí. La ceremonia, que se celebrará este domingo 15 de marzo y será presentada por Conan O’Brien. Esta edición no solo definirá lo mejor del cine, también determinará el destino de decenas de millones de dólares en los crecientes mercados de predicción. De momento, la película que lidera todas las apuestas es “One Battle After Another”.
Desde que se anunciaron los nominados en enero, plataformas como Polymarket y Kalshi han estado repletas de predicciones.
Apostadores de todo el mundo han estado negociando con las probabilidades de las 24 categorías. Este, sin duda, es un fenómeno que ha captado la atención de cientos de medios. El historial de estos mercados es cada vez más respetado; de hecho, Polymarket acertó en 26 de las 28 categorías en los Golden Globes de este año.
Si las probabilidades actuales son correctas, la gran triunfadora de la noche será “One Battle After Another”, la nueva película de Paul Thomas Anderson, que se llevaría cuatro estatuillas, incluyendo las más importantes.
“One Battle After Another”, la gran favorita de la noche
La película lidera las apuestas en las categorías más importantes. Para Mejor Película, se le otorga una contundente probabilidad de alrededor del 75 %, con más de $44 millones apostados en su victoria. Su director, Paul Thomas Anderson, es también el favorito indiscutible para llevarse el Mejor Director, con un 90 % de posibilidades.
El dominio de la cinta se extiende a categorías técnicas y de guion. Es la favorita para ganar el Oscar a Mejor Fotografía (76 %), Mejor Guion Adaptado (más del 95 %) y Mejor Montaje (80 %). Además, Sean Penn, quien actúa en la película, es el principal candidato a llevarse el premio al Mejor Actor de Reparto, con un 68 % de probabilidades.
La competencia: “Sinners” y “Frankenstein” también brillan
Aunque “One Battle After Another” parte como favorita, no estará sola en el podio. Se espera que “Sinners”, de Ryan Coogler, y “Frankenstein”, de Guillermo del Toro, se queden con al menos tres premios cada una.
“Sinners” parece imparable en las categorías de sonido y guion. Es la candidata número uno a Mejor Banda Sonora Original (93 %), Mejor Guion Original (97 %) y Mejor Reparto (75 %).
Su actor principal, Michael B. Jordan, también es el favorito en una competida categoría de Mejor Actor, con aproximadamente un 47 % de posibilidades, después de darle la vuelta a las predicciones iniciales que daban como ganador a Timothée Chalamet.
Por su parte, “Frankenstein” domina las categorías artísticas y de maquillaje. Es la gran favorita para ganar los premios a Mejor Diseño de Producción, Mejor Diseño de Vestuario y Mejor Maquillaje y Peluquería, rondando todas ellas el 90% de probabilidades.
Otras categorías destacadas
En el resto de categorías, los mercados de predicción también tienen claros sus favoritos:
- Mejor Actriz: Jessie Buckley (“Hamnet”) es la ganadora casi asegurada, con un 96% de posibilidades.
- Mejor Actor de Reparto: La actriz Amy Madigan (“Weapons”) lidera las apuestas con un 47%, tras un vuelco en las predicciones que inicialmente favorecían a Teyana Taylor.
- Mejores Efectos Visuales: “Avatar: Fire and Ash” es la ganadora indiscutible, con más de un 90% de probabilidades.
- Mejor Sonido: La película de F1, protagonizada por Brad Pitt, es la gran favorita para llevarse esta categoría técnica (80%).
- Mejor Canción Original: “Golden”, el éxito viral de “KPop Demon Hunters”, es la clara favorita con un 80% de opciones.
- Mejor Película de Animación: “KPop Demon Hunters” repite como favorita en esta categoría, con un 92% de probabilidades.
- Mejor Cortometraje de Animación: Es la categoría con más incertidumbre. “Butterfly” lidera con un 50%, seguido de cerca por “La chica que lloraba perlas” (27-30%).
Los mercados de predicción han hablado. Solo queda esperar a la noche del domingo para ver si, una vez más, aciertan o si los Premios Oscar deparan alguna sorpresa. La ceremonia se podrá ver en vivo por ABC y Hulu.

sources.news_title: Giorgio Armani’s Annual Pre-Oscars Cocktail Party in Beverly Hills Was As Stylish As It Sounds
sources.text:
Giorgio Armani’s Annual Pre-Oscars Cocktail Party in Beverly Hills Was as Stylish as It Sounds
On the eve of the Oscars 2026, the Hollywood Hills were alive with the sound of clinking glasses, celebrating another successful year of film and the industry’s top talent. And when it comes to stylish soirees, no one does it quite like Giorgio Armani. On Saturday evening, Rodeo Drive was abuzz as an exclusive guest list gathered at the flagship boutique for the label’s annual cocktail party—a happy hour like no other, with no shortage of style and star power.
Just after 5 p.m., Heated Rivalry heartthrobs François Arnaud and Robbie G.K. were among the first to arrive through a throng of fans and onlookers swarming outside the store. Both looked sharp in all-black Armani looks, with Robbie G.K. opting for a tailored blazer and trousers and Arnaud in a collarless silk striped shirt and velvet pants. “When I went in for my fitting, this was the first thing I touched,” Robbie G.K. told Vogue of the winning ensemble. “I tried this on immediately, and that was it. That was all I needed to know.” Meanwhile, Arnaud had a particular reference in mind: “My look was a nod to one of my favorite movies of all time, Beetlejuice,” he laughed. “An Armani fitting is hard because everything fits so perfectly. But this was the most different from what I’d worn before.”
It wasn’t long before the Michael Chow–designed flagship’s main floor was filled with famous faces. Weaving through the crowd were Ginnifer Goodwin and Kerry Condon, who could be seen sipping cocktails and mingling with guests, while Abbott Elementary’s Janelle James browsed the Armani Beauty counter in a long-sleeve LBD that she said was an ode to her native New Yorker style. Across the room, Minnie Driver showed off one of the most unique designs of the night: a black velvet tank featuring a crystal-embellished portrait of the late Giorgio Armani. “It’s a pretty snazzy top,” Driver said. “I also think, in a weekend where I am wearing a lot of big dresses, I wanted to wear pants and a top.”
Around 6:30 p.m. a frenzy of fans clamored around the Armani doors, marking the superstar-like arrival of Hudson Williams. Greeting members of the Armani team with warm hugs, the actor made his way to the upper level, joining fellow Canadian and Love Story star Paul Anthony Kelly, who had taken a leaf from John F. Kennedy Jr.’s ’90s-style playbook in a double-breasted suit.
On the suspended balcony, Macaulay Culkin danced with his wife, Brenda Song, playfully spinning her around to show off their matching sleek black looks. “We wanted to be casual but chic,” Song said, while Culkin flashed his matching noir-painted manicure. Song and Culkin weren’t the only ones enjoying an Armani date night. It was a Landman reunion for Jon Hamm and Ali Larter, who were accompanied by their respective spouses, Anna Osceola and Hayes MacArthur. Samuel L. Jackson and his wife, LaTanya Richardson Jackson, also joined the party and were spotted taking photos with their goddaughter, Jurnee Smollett. “Armani is just effortlessly sexy,” Larter said of her sleeveless gown, equipped with an embellished cage-knit bodice. “A lot of the time, I’m corseted in and everything’s tight and uncomfortable, but this is just easy—and I feel cool.”
Armani’s effortless, easy-to-wear elegance seemed to be the theme of the night for all guests, including Yara Shahidi. “I like to feel like, Oh, this is something I would actually wear,” she told Vogue of choosing her look, a draped, forest green top with matching chiffon pants. “It has to feel like an extension of you.”

sources.news_title: It's 'Sinners' vs 'One Battle' as the Oscars begin | ABS-CBN Entertainment
Press advocacy group plans to protest David Ellison's takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery
sources.text:
Oscars 2026 highlights: 'One Battle After Another' wins best picture; Michael B. Jordan wins for 'Sinners'
The 98th Academy Awards, which took place at the Dolby Theatre at Ovation Hollywood, aired on ABC and streamed on Hulu.
And that's a wrap on Oscars 2026. What to know:
- Lights, camera, Conan: Conan O’Brien returned to host the Oscars for a second year, taking the stage of the Dolby Theatre after A-list stars braved the red carpet in 80-degree Los Angeles weather. He dressed as nominee Amy Madigan's "Weapons" character, Aunt Gladys, for the opening segment, which featured a tribute to the nominated films. For his hosting efforts, he was jokingly given the short-lived title of "host for life" in a post-awards scene.
- It was a big night for Warner Bros. Discovery: Paul Thomas Anderson’s “One Battle After Another,” which was nominated in 13 categories, dominated the show, taking home six, including the coveted best picture. Ryan Coogler’s “Sinners,” which made Oscar history with 16 nominations, followed with four awards. The wins for Warner Bros. come as the media conglomerate is preparing to merge with Paramount Skydance, the company owned by David Ellison.
- Making history: Autumn Durald Arkapaw became the first woman to win the best cinematography Oscar for her work in "Sinners." After thanking Coogler, she asked all the women in the room to stand up. "I feel like I don't get here without you guys," she said.
- An emotional In Memoriam: Billy Crystal took the stage early in the evening to honor his late best friend, Rob Reiner, and his wife, Michele. His speech kicked off the segment that paid tribute to industry giants who died in the last year. Rachel McAdams also spoke about late stars, including her "fellow Canadian" Catherine O'Hara and her "Family Stone" co-star Diane Keaton, whom she described as "a legend with no end." Barbra Streisand also spoke about Robert Redford before singing a song from their classic film together, "The Way We Were."
And the final Oscar goes to ...
Everyone who made it through this awards season.
2026 Oscars: A quick video recap
If you didn't have 3½ hours to spare, NBC News' video team has you covered with a less-than-three-minute video recap of tonight's show.
Watch below:
ICYMI: Michael B. Jordan's acceptance speech
The best actor winner thanked Ryan Coogler, his parents and Warner Bros. in his speech.
An In Memoriam to remember
The In Memoriam segment featured tributes from actors Billy Crystal, Rachel McAdams and Barbra Streisand.
Warner Bros. comes out on top
Warner Bros. won big tonight, taking home 11 total Oscars (six for "One Battle After Another," four for "Sinners" and one for "Weapons").
Netflix followed with seven wins (including three for "Frankenstein" and two for "KPop Demon Hunters").
Who won the most Oscars? A final tally of the biggest winners of the night
- "One Battle After Another": 6
- "Sinners": 4
- "Frankenstein": 3
- "KPop Demon Hunters": 2
Ejae had something to say about being cut off during her acceptance speech
After winning best original song for “Golden,” Ejae noted that she wanted to say more onstage about the collaborative effort behind “KPop Demon Hunters,” but “I didn’t get to because they just cut us off.”
“But I wanted to thank Rei Ami and Audrey Nuna,” Ejae told reporters backstage. “They killed it with their singing. And they’re just incredible people, and I love them so much.”
The Oscars ended with one last Conan bit
After the final award of the night, the Oscars ended with a recorded skit.
Spoofing the end of “One Battle After Another,” actor and comedian Jim Downey presented Conan O’Brien with his own office as Oscars Host For Life.
We won’t spoil the end of the movie here, but it didn’t end well for Conan after he stepped into his office. The new host for life was then revealed to be Mr. Beast.
Paul Thomas Anderson celebrates 'wonderful, wonderful journey'
Paul Thomas Anderson, accepting the best picture Oscar for "One Battle After Another," highlighted the five seminal films nominated in the category in 1976: "Dog Day Afternoon," "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest," "Jaws," "Nashville" and "Barry Lyndon."
"There is no best among of them," Anderson said, suggesting that he felt similarly about this year's crop of contenders.
He thanked his crew and crew, celebrating the "wonderful, wonderful journey" of making and promoting the film.
‘One Battle’ prevails in a close best picture showdown
Paul Thomas Anderson’s “One Battle After Another” has been named best picture at the 98th Academy Awards, closing the curtains on one of the most competitive Oscar battles in years.
Anderson’s portrait of faded leftist revolutionaries on the run from a ruthless military officer beat “Sinners,” Ryan Coogler’s genre-bending vampire epic, and eight other contenders.
“One Battle” nabbed a grand total of six awards, including best director and best adapted screenplay for Anderson, who drew inspiration from the Thomas Pynchon novel “Vineland.”
Best picture winner
“One Battle After Another”
'Moulin Rogue' hive rise up
Thank you, academy, for bringing together Ewan McGregor and Nicole Kidman to present.
If only they could serenade us with "Moulin Rogue" jams for longer than a minute.
Jessie Buckley bursts into tears as she accepts award
Jessie Buckley immediately began crying after her name was announced as that of the best actress winner for her performance in “Hamnet.”
“Thank you to the incredible women I stand beside. I’m inspired by your art and your heart,” Buckley said of her fellow nominees.
Buckley thanked her director, Chloé Zhao, for allowing her to “understand the capacity of a mother’s love” and also gave emotional thanks to her husband.
Buckley ended her speech by thanking mothers.
“It’s Mother’s Day in the U.K. today. I would like to dedicate this to the beautiful chaos of a mother's heart,” she said. “We all come from a lineage of women who continue to create against all odds.”
'Sinners' cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw says her win ‘isn’t about me anymore’
Autumn Durald Arkapaw, the first woman to win best cinematography in Oscars history, said backstage that she wanted to thank all the women in the room “because moments like this don’t happen without women standing up for you and advocating for you.”
“I’ve learned over the past few months going through this process that it does take a village to make stuff like this happen," she said. "But this isn’t about me anymore. This is about so much more, and I know that, and I wanted it for all the ladies in the room, and I wanted it for all the girls at home.”
Jessie Buckley has swept awards season
Jessie Buckley’s victory for her role as a grieving mother in Chloé Zhao’s “Hamnet” completes her clean sweep of awards season. She previously won equivalent honors at the Golden Globes, the Critics’ Choice Awards, SAG’s Actor Awards and the British Academy Film Awards.
Buckley, 36, broke onto the scene just eight years ago with 2018’s “Wild Rose.” She nabbed her first Oscar nomination three years later, for Maggie Gyllenhaal’s “The Lost Daughter,” and appeared in the acclaimed ensemble drama “Women Talking.”
Actress in a leading role winner
Jessie Buckley, “Hamnet”
Michael B. Jordan pays tribute to previous Black Oscar winners
Jordan, taking the Dolby Theatre main stage to thunderous applause and a standing ovation, told the crowd: "God is good."
He recognized his mother and father sitting in the theater, thanked the team at Warner Bros. for "betting on original ideas" and extended his gratitude to longtime collaborator Ryan Coogler.
"I stand here because of the people that came before me," Jordan said, highlighting Black Oscar winners such as Sidney Poitier, Denzel Washington, Halle Barry, Forrest Whittaker and Will Smith.
The room goes wild for Michael B. Jordan
The "Sinners" star got a rousing reaction in the Dolby Theatre after taking home the best actor award.
It was the most competitive best actor race in years
Michael B. Jordan’s victory for his dual performance as twin brothers in “Sinners” was by no means a sure thing. The fight for the best actor trophy was fiercely competitive this year, pitting Jordan against formidable contenders like Timothée Chalamet (“Marty Supreme”) and Wagner Moura (“The Secret Agent”).
Chalamet picked up early momentum after scooping up prizes from the Golden Globes and the Critics’ Choice Awards. But the vibes seemed to shift after Jordan pulled an upset at the Screen Actors Guild’s Actor Awards. Chalamet, meanwhile, spent recent weeks at the center of an internet firestorm over his comments about the cultural relevance of ballet and opera.
Jordan’s triumph caps off an incredible ascent for an actor who first made an impression as a teenager on HBO’s “The Wire” in the early 2000s. Jordan’s tight collaboration with “Sinners” writer-director Ryan Coogler now spans five films, including the “Rocky” reboot “Creed” and the box-office smash “Black Panther.”
Next up for “MBJ” is a remake of “The Thomas Crown Affair” for Amazon MGM Studios. He’s pulling double duty as leading man and director.

Anderson was previously nominated in this category for “There Will Be Blood,” “Phantom Thread” and “Licorice Pizza.” Yet despite his stature, the industry’s top directing prize eluded him — until tonight.

Trier also paid tribute to the four other films nominated in the international film category and ended his speech by paraphrasing James Baldwin, saying in part that all adults are responsible for all the world's children.

Bardem, 57, has been especially outspoken about the Palestinians over the last few years amid the ongoing war in Gaza.
How one indie label conquered the international film race
“Sentimental Value,” “It Was Just an Accident,” “The Secret Agent” and “Sirāt” have something in common. They all premiered at last year’s prestigious Cannes Film Festival, where they were acquired for U.S. theatrical distribution by Neon, a nine-year-old company that has swiftly established itself as a force to be reckoned with in modern independent film.
Neon released two of the last six winners of the best picture Oscar: Bong Joon Ho’s “Parasite” and Sean Baker’s “Anora.” But even more notably, Neon has dominated Cannes for six consecutive years, winning the coveted Palme d’Or for “It Was Just an Accident,” “Anora,” “Anatomy of a Fall,” “Triangle of Sadness,” “Titane” and “Parasite.”
“Sentimental Value,” a Norwegian drama about an actor’s estrangement from her filmmaker father, went into the night with the clearest momentum. But it faced stiff competition from Iranian auteur Jafar Panahi’s “It Was Just an Accident” and Brazilian director Kleber Mendonça Filho’s “The Secret Agent,” which both examine life under repressive government regimes.
The fifth entry in this year’s international feature race was Tunisia’s “The Voice of Hind Rajab,” a docudrama about the killing of a 6-year-old Palestinian girl in Gaza.

Autumn Durald Arkapaw is first woman to win cinematography Oscar
Durald Arkapaw just made history.
Her work for "Sinners" has made her the first woman to win the Oscar for cinematography. She is also the first Black cinematographer to to win this award.
She said she felt like she had to meet director Ryan Coogler to win this award, whom she worked with on the 2022 Marvel film “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever.”
After thanking Coogler, she went on to call all the women in the room to stand to celebrate the award with her.
"I really want all the women in the room to stand up, because I feel like I don't get here without you guys," she said. "I have felt so much love from all the women on this campaign ... and I just feel like moments like this happen because of you guys."

There's more to the Oscars than just the show
Academy President Lynette Howell Taylor highlighted some less glitzy components of the Oscars: scientific and technical awards, Governors Awards and the Academy Museum, which is in Los Angeles.
The Governors Awards, which are selected by the academy’s board based on artists’ careers, are distinct from the competitive Academy Awards given out during the Oscars show tonight.

Filmmaker says winning doc is about 'how you lose your country'
In his Oscar acceptance speech, filmmaker David Borenstein said "Mr. Nobody Against Putin" is a documentary about "how you lose your country."
"You lose through small little acts of complicity," Borenstein said, such as "when we don't say anything, when oligarchs take over the media and control how we produce it and consume it."
"But luckily, even a nobody can do something about it," Borenstein said before he passed the microphone to the film's subject and co-director, Pavel Talankin.
"In the name of our future, in the name of all of our children, stop all of these wars now," Talankin said.
Three of the last four documentary winners concern Russia
Three of the last four films to win the documentary feature prize at the Oscars relate to modern Russia under President Vladimir Putin.
"Navalny," 2023's winner, centered on the late Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny. "20 Days in Mariupol," 2024's winner, chronicled the first weeks of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
"Mr. Nobody Against Putin," this year's winner, follows an everyday schoolteacher who takes a stand against the Russian regime.
Uvalde mom speaks after award for documentary short
“All the Empty Rooms,” a short film about children who were killed in school shootings, won the award for documentary short.
One of the recipients of the award was the mother of a child killed in the elementary school shooting in Uvalde, Texas, in 2022.
“Since that day, her bedroom has been frozen in time,” Gloria Cazares said. “Jackie is more than just a headline. She is our light and life. Gun violence is now the No. 1 cause of death in kids and teens. We believe if the world could see their empty bedrooms, we'd be a different America.”

Cameron has plans for additional “Avatar” films, although it's not clear whether he'll make them — even though the existing three films have grossed billions of dollars.

Analysis: Ryan Coogler’s towering stature in modern Hollywood
Ryan Coogler had already made history before the ceremony when his fifth feature, “Sinners,” racked up a commanding 16 nominations — the most of any single film in the 98-year history of the Academy Awards. Coogler’s victory tonight in the best original screenplay field cements his status as one of the key writer-directors in modern Hollywood.
Coogler made his feature debut in 2013 with the wrenching drama “Fruitvale Station,” kicking off a rewarding collaboration with actor Michael B. Jordan that some critics have likened to Martin Scorsese’s long partnerships with Robert De Niro and Leonard DiCaprio. Coogler’s next projects were “Creed” and the culture-conquering box-office phenomenon “Black Panther.”
It remains to be seen whether “Sinners,” one of last year’s undisputed critical and commercial sensations, takes home the best picture and best director prizes at the end of the night. But regardless of what happens, Coogler is clearly a defining voice in modern cinema.
