Conan O'Brien va vous servir les Oscars sur un plateau
L'humoriste rempile dans son rôle de maître de cérémonie. Autodérision, humour absurde et actualité au menu de la 98e soirée des Oscars.
- Publié le 15-03-2026 à 13h40
Jusqu'à la dernière minute, il va guetter l'actualité, riche en "rebondissements" ces derniers jours. Car si Conan O'Brien ne veut pas transformer la cérémonie des Oscars en une tribune politique, il tient à ce que son monologue d'ouverture soit en phase avec l'état du monde. Décrit comme un humoriste cérébral, le natif de Brookline (Massachusetts), où il vit le jour le 18 avril 1963, sort diplômé de Harvard (en histoire américaine) en 1985. Le grand (1,93 m) rouquin a fait ses armes au sein du magazine humoristique du campus et c'est tout naturellement qu'il poursuit l'aventure en rejoignant l'équipe du Saturday Night Live, à la fin des années 80.
C'est ensuite à la famille de Bart Simpson qu'il se consacre, signant quelques épisodes devenus culte. Ses références parfois absurdes, son goût pour l'autodérision et son sens aigu du tempo comique lui valent de prendre la succession de David Letterman, avec son Late Night With Conan O'Brien. Les trois premières années sont semées d'embûches mais dès 1997, l'émission – l'une des plus suivies aux États-Unis – est couverte d'éloges et de récompenses.
En 2009, c'est à un autre monstre de la télévision américaine qu'il succède : Jay Leno. Mais l'aventure du Tonight Show sera de courte durée, l'animateur choisissant une autre chaîne mais un concept similaire avec Conan. Il peut y apposer sa griffe, celle du chaos comique qu'il aime entretenir. Des blagues qui tombent à plat, des ratages bien maîtrisés, le tout servi par son grand corps dégingandé : le public est conquis.
C'est aussi cela qui a séduit l'Academy Awards qui, en 2025, lui offrait d'être le maître de la cérémonie des Oscars. En artisan méticuleux du gag, il s'efforce de se moquer de l'industrie du cinéma tout en la célébrant. Un grand écart payant puisque le revoici aux commandes. Il y a quelques jours, Conan a mis du sien en déroulant le tapis rouge de la cérémonie, au sens littéral du terme. Depuis, laissant de côté pour quelque temps son podcast hyperpopulaire Conan O'Brien Needs a Friend, auquel il se consacre depuis son départ des petits écrans, l'humoriste scrute à la loupe l'actualité et peaufine les blagues qu'il servira au gratin d'Hollywood, dimanche à Los Angeles.

sources.news_title: Oscar, Crowd of Stars at the Event of Giorgio Armani
sources.text:
(di Lucia Magi)
Sfilata di stelle al
tradizionale cocktail pre-Oscar di Giorgio Armani su Rodeo
Drive: Jon Hamm, Samuel L. Jackson, Macaulay Culkin, ma anche il
divo nuovo di zecca Paul Anthony Kelly, scoperto da Ryan Murphy
per il ruolo di John John Kennedy nella serie 'Love Story', in
onda su Disney+. L'esclusivo appuntamento a Beverly Hills
celebra i candidati agli Oscar e gli "amici" (come li descrive
Vanity Fair) della maison italiana.
Quest'anno l'evento ha assunto anche il sapore di un omaggio
a Re Giorgio, scomparso lo scorso settembre. Fuori dalle vetrine
alte due piani della boutique, il traffico era congestionato di
auto nere e una piccola folla di curiosi e fan stava accalcata
dietro le transenne disposte sul marciapiede.
Oltre a Hamm - di ritorno sul piccolo schermo il 3 aprile con
la seconda stagione di 'Your Friends & Neighbors' - e all'attore
di Quentin Tarantino Samuel L. Jackson, tra gli invitati c'erano
anche Kerry Condon, che ha interpretato la direttrice tecnica
nel film 'F1', candidato come miglior film, e Minnie Driver
('Will Hunting - Genio ribelle').
Tra calici di champagne, vassoi di leggeri finger food,
manichini e scansie con le creazioni della casa, si muovevano
con un nugolo di assistenti e amici anche Hudson Williams, noto
per il ruolo di Shane Hollander nella serie 'Heated Rivalry' e
Auliʻi Cravalho, che ha dato la voce alla protagonista di
Oceania 1 e 2, nella versione originale. L'ex bambino di 'Mamma,
ho perso l'aereo', visto recentemente nella seconda stagione di
'Fallout', è arrivato con la moglie e collega Brenda Song.
Avvistati anche Josh Duhamel - celebre per il ruolo del
colonnello William Lennox nella saga di 'Transformers' - e la
moglie Audra Mari, alla loro prima apparizione pubblica dopo
aver annunciato una settimana fa di aspettare il secondo figlio.
Tra gli ospiti anche l''attrice italiana Beatrice Grannò, che
interpretava Mia nella seconda stagione della serie 'The White
Lotus'.

Oscars 2026: Priyanka Chopra joins high-profile line-up of presenters - The Tribune
sources.text:
Oscars 2026: Priyanka Chopra joins high-profile line-up of presenters
The ceremony will mark a return to the Oscar stage for host Conan O'Brien, whose comedic style and sharp satire have long been staples of American late-night television
The 98th edition of the Academy Awards will unfold on Sunday, March 15, 2026, at the iconic Dolby Theatre in Ovation Hollywood, bringing together some of the film industry's biggest names for a ceremony that blends tradition, innovation and a new milestone for filmmaking recognition.
Hosted by late-night comedian and television personality Conan O'Brien, the ceremony will be broadcast live at 5 pm PT/8 pm ET on ABC and streamed on Hulu.
With a packed lineup of presenters, strong contenders across major categories, and the introduction of a new award recognising casting directors, the 2026 Oscars promise to be a landmark night for Hollywood.
The Academy has assembled a high-profile roster of presenters for the evening. Among those expected to take the stage are actors Robert Downey Jr., Anne Hathaway, Nicole Kidman, Pedro Pascal, Sigourney Weaver, Priyanka Chopra and Ewan McGregor.
The ceremony will mark a return to the Oscar stage for host Conan O'Brien, whose comedic style and sharp satire have long been staples of American late-night television. Organisers have indicated that the opening segment will feature a globally themed film sequence, setting the tone for an internationally focused celebration of cinema, as per The Hollywood Reporter.
This year's race is headlined by several films that have dominated the awards conversation.
In the Best Picture category, leading contenders include 'One Battle After Another', 'Sinners', 'Bugonia', 'Hamnet,' 'Marty Supreme,' and 'Frankenstein.' Among them, 'One Battle After Another', directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, has drawn particular attention as the filmmaker seeks his first Oscar win after previously earning 11 nominations.
Another major contender is 'Sinners', directed by Ryan Coogler and starring Michael B. Jordan. The film blends supernatural horror with historical storytelling and has received strong recognition for its performances and atmosphere.
Meanwhile, 'Hamnet,' helmed by Chloe Zhao, has emerged as a powerful literary adaptation, praised for its emotional storytelling and period detail.
Other notable titles in the Best Picture lineup include 'Bugonia', directed by Yorgos Lanthimos, the stylised drama 'Marty Supreme' from Josh Safdie, and 'Frankenstein', directed by Guillermo del Toro.
The Best Actor race is widely regarded as one of the most competitive in recent years. Nominees include Michael B. Jordan for 'Sinners', Timothee Chalamet for 'Marty Supreme', and Leonardo DiCaprio for 'One Battle After Another.' In the Best Actress category, strong contenders include Jessie Buckley for 'Hamnet', Emma Stone for 'Bugonia,' and Rose Byrne for 'If I Had Legs I'd Kick You.' For the first time in Oscar history, the Academy will present an award for Best Casting. The category recognises the work of casting directors who assemble the ensembles behind major films.
Among the inaugural nominees are Francine Maisler for 'Sinners', Cassandra Kulukundis for 'One Battle After Another', Nina Gold for 'Hamnet,' Jennifer Venditti for 'Marty Supreme', and Gabriel Domingues for 'The Secret Agent.' The introduction of the category marks a significant shift for the Academy, acknowledging a department that has long played a central role in shaping the success of films.
This year's ceremony also places a strong emphasis on environmental sustainability. The Academy has introduced several eco-friendly initiatives, including energy-efficient LED lighting, rechargeable batteries used across the production, and a fully recyclable red carpet.
The evening's entertainment will include performances connected to nominated films, particularly music from 'Sinners.' A special appearance by K-Pop artist EJAE is also expected, as per The Hollywood Reporter.
Just a few days before the Oscars 2026, the creative team has also teased epic 'Bridesmaids' and 'Marvel' reunions at the awards.
"There's been rumours of what that reunion is, and we are very excited to announce that we have a Bridesmaids reunion that is going to be very special," said Oscars executive producer Raj Kapoor.
Executive producer Katy Mullan further added, "There's also going to be a Marvel reunion for the superhero fans, so we're going to have superstars and superheroes. And there is also going to be an extraterrestrial on the stage, so you can figure that one out."
The 98th Oscars will air Sunday, with the creative team promising a mix of nostalgia, star power and musical spectacle.

sources.news_title: 98th Academy Awards: A 'Sinners' and 'One Battle After Another' showdown
sources.text:
LOS ANGELES — Happy Oscars Sunday to all who celebrate.
"One Battle After Another" took home six Oscars, including best director and best adapted screenplay, the Oscars' first trophy for best casting and best supporting actor for an absent Sean Penn.
Related Stories
- Jessie Buckley won best actress and Michael B. Jordan won best actor at the 98th Academy Awards
- “Sinners” cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw has made Oscar history, becoming the first female director of photography to win the award in the 98-year history of the Academy Awards
- Moving tributes were paid to Robert Redford, Diane Keaton and Rob Reiner
- The Oscar night belonged to Warner Bros., the studio of “One Battle After Another” and “Sinners”
"Sinners" took home Best Actor for Michael B. Jordan, Best Score, Best Cinematography.
Jessie Buckley won best actress for "Hamnet."
Conan O’Brien kicked off the 98th Academy Awards Sunday night with a montage of clips from Best Picture nominees while taking on Amy Madigan’s Aunt Gladys from “Weapons” as kids ran behind him.
O’Brien didn’t wait to hold back. He instantly joked about a Waymo hosting next year’s ceremony in a tux. He took a swing at Timothée Chalamet’s recent controversial remarks about opera and ballet.
No awards show is complete without a musical performance.
Miles Caton and Raphael Saadiq performed “I Lied to You,” the nominated original song from “Sinners.” They were joined by a bevy of performers onstage — Misty Copeland, Eric Gales, Buddy Guy, Brittany Howard, Christone “Kingfish” Ingram, Jayme Lawson, Li Jun Li, Bobby Rush, Shaboozey and Alice Smith among them — for a near-recreation of the scene in “Sinners” where the song is introduced.
It is one of the more memorable moments in the film, where a blues song in a Mississippi juke joint opens up to showcase hip-hop DJs, rock ‘n’ roll guitarists, ballerinas and more, illustrating the Black music genre’s place at the foundation of American popular culture.
When the live tribute performance to “Sinners” wrapped on stage, there was a slew of applause, some of which came from people who stood for the ovation.
One of the most highly expected reunions of the night was that of the cast of “Bridesmaids.” Melissa McCarthy, Kristen Wiig, Rose Byrne, Ellie Kemper and Maya Rudolph come together to present during the ceremony.
Did we get a “The Devil Wears Prada” reunion? Sort of ... Anna Wintour and Anne Hathaway teamed up to present the costume design and make and hairstyling Oscars.
Billy Crystal opened the in memoriam segment honoring his best friend, Rob Reiner.
He ticked off a list of Reiner’s films, including “When Harry Met Sally,” starring Crystal and Meg Ryan, “Stand By Me,” “Say Anything” and “This is Spinal Tap,” among many others.
A photo of Reiner and his wife, Michelle Singer Reiner, appeared behind Crystal.
The Reiners were found dead in their Los Angeles home in December. Their son, Nick Reiner, has been charged in the deaths of his parents and has pleaded not guilty.
Having a slew of actors with longstanding ties to Reiner — Meg Ryan, Kiefer Sutherland, Fred Savage, Demi Moore, John Cusack, Ione Skye and many others — come on stage for the tribute was reminiscent of how the Academy did the same for director John Hughes at the Oscars 16 years ago.
Here’s a list of all the nominees. Winners will be in bold as they are announced throughout the ceremony.
Best Picture
- "Bugonia"
- "F1"
- "Frankenstein"
- "Hamnet"
- "Marty Supreme"
- "One Battle After Another"
- "The Secret Agent"
- "Sentimental Value"
- "Sinners"
- "Train Dreams"
"Getting to make this film with this cast and this crew and Paul, has already been the greatest filmmaking experience I can fathom. So, receiving this award is just beyond. My heart is exploding with gratitude. Thank you," said film producer Sara Murphy during her Academy Award acceptance speech.
"I really blew it when I won a Best Director award and I forgot to thank my cast. With Leo, Benicio, Teyana, Sean, Regina, and especially Chase, my American girl, Chase. You are the heart of this movie, this entire team. What a night, you guys!" said Anderson.
Best Actor
- Timothée Chalamet, "Marty Supreme"
- Leonardo DiCaprio, "One Battle After Another"
- Ethan Hawke, "Blue Moon"
- Michael B. Jordan, "Sinners"
- Wagner Moura, "The Secret Agent"
"God is good," said Jordan as he accepted his Oscar.
"Y'all. I stand here because of the people that came before me: Sidney Poitier, Denzel Washington, Halle Berry, Jamie Foxx, Forest Whitaker, Will Smith. To be amongst those giants, amongst those greats, amongst my ancestors, amongst my guys," he said during his acceptance speech. "Thank you, everybody in this room and everybody at home for supporting me over my career. I feel it. I know you guys want me to do well. And I want to do that because you guys bet on me. So thank you for keep betting on me. And I'm going to keep stepping up."
Jordan is the sixth Black man to win the best actor trophy. He joins Will Smith (“King Richard,” 2020), Forest Whitaker (“The Last King of Scotland,” 2006), Jamie Foxx (“Ray,” 2004), Denzel Washington (“Training Day,” 2001) and Sidney Poitier (“Lillies of the Field”), who was the first in 1963.
Best Supporting Actor
- Benicio Del Toro, "One Battle After Another"
- Jacob Elordi, "Frankenstein"
- Delroy Lindo, "Sinners"
- Sean Penn, "One Battle After Another"
- Stellan Skarsgard, "Sentimental Value"
Penn did not attend Sunday night's ceremony.
The win marks Penn’s third Academy Award.
The actor did attend when he previously won two Academy Awards for best actor for Clint Eastwood’s 2003 crime drama “Mystic River” and for portraying San Francisco politician and LGBTQ rights pioneer Harvey Milk in Gus Van Sant’s 2008 biopic “Milk.”
Best Actress
- Jessie Buckley, "Hamnet"
- Rose Byrne, "If I Had Legs I'd Kick You"
- Kate Hudson, "Song Sung Blue"
- Renate Reinsve, "Sentimental Value"
- Emma Stone, "Bugonia"
The Oscar win makes her the first Irish performer to ever win in the category.
"It's Mother's Day in the U.K. today. So, I would like to dedicate this to the beautiful chaos of a mother's heart. We all come from a lineage of women who continue to create against all odds. Thank you for recognizing me in this role. This is the greatest honor. I can't even believe it," she said during her acceptance speech.
Best Supporting Actress
- Elle Fanning, "Sentimental Value"
- Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas, "Sentimental Value"
- Amy Madigan, "Weapons"
- Wunmi Mosaku, "Sinners"
- Teyana Taylor, "One Battle After Another"
“Thank you very much. I am very overwhelmed,” said Madigan as she accepted her Oscar.
When answering press questions, Madigan said, "I loved the script as soon as I read it. I knew I could grab it by the throat."
Madigan also hinted a potential prequel to "Weapons."
The last time she was nominated for an Oscar was for her role in 1985 family drama “Twice in a Lifetime,” setting a record for the longest gap between nominations for an actress.
Best Director
- Chloé Zhao, "Hamnet"
- Josh Safdie, "Marty Supreme"
- Paul Thomas Anderson, "One Battle After Another"
- Joachim Trier, "Sentimental Value"
- Ryan Coogler, "Sinners"
"Thank you very, very, very much. You make a guy work hard for one of these. I really appreciate it. I share this with a friend of mine on the other side of the shadows. His name, Adam Somner," said Anderson as he accepted his Oscar.
"I'm here because of people's faith in me. They give me their faith and their time. And that's the best part about being on a film crew. Is being with people. Cause we need each other. This is a wonderful gift, and I'm so happy to call the movies home," he added.
Best Animated Feature Film
- "Arco"
- "Elio"
- "KPop Demon Hunters"
- "Little Amélie or the Character of Rain"
- "Zootopia 2"
“This is for Korea and for Koreans everywhere,” said co-director Maggie Kang as she received her Academy Award.
"Thank you to the Academy and to all the fans who got us here. And for those of you who look like me, I'm so sorry that it took us so long to see us in a movie like this. But it is here. And that means that the next generations don't have to go longing," she added.
Best Animated Short Film
- "Butterfly"
- "Forevergreen"
- "The Girl Who Cried Pearls"
- "Retirement Plan"
- "The Three Sisters"
"I guess, people think it takes patience to take five years to make a puppet film. It actually takes patience to live with someone who takes five years to make a puppet film. So, I'd like to thank my wife, Maya, and my daughter, Tulli," said Chris Lavis as he accepted his award.
Maciek Szczerbowski, who won with Lavis, said, "We just really want to thank our amazing neighborhood, and the amazingly talented community of artists that we've had the superb luck to work with. Thank you, the fantastic city of Montreal. Thank you, Canada."
Casting
- "Hamnet," Nina Gold
- "Marty Supreme," Jennifer Venditti
- "One Battle After Another," Cassandra Kulukundis
- "The Secret Agent," Gabriel Domingues
- "Sinners," Francine Maisler
“I dedicate this to you and to the casting directors who never got a chance to get up here, who didn’t even get a chance to get their name on the movie," said Kulukundis when she accepted her Oscar.
Cinematography
- "Frankenstein," Dan Laustsen
- "Marty Supreme," Darius Khondji
- "One Battle After Another," Michael Bauman
- "Sinners," Autumn Durald Arkapaw
- "Train Dreams," Adolpho Veloso
Arkapaw becomes first woman and Black person to win the award.
“I really want all the women in this room to stand up, because I feel like I don’t get here without you guys.”
The crowd began applauding as the women in the audience got on their feet.
"A lot of little girls that look like me will be able to sleep well tonight because they'll be able to become cinematographers," Arkapaw told media after accepting her Oscar.
Costume Design
- "Avatar: Fire and Ash," Deborah L. Scott
- "Frankenstein," Kate Hawley
- "Hamnet," Malgosia Turzanska
- "Marty Supreme," Miyako Bellizzi
- "Sinners," Ruth E. Carter
“On behalf of myself and the amazing team that I work with, the artisans, the alchemists, dream weavers, we’re so grateful to the Academy for recognizing our craft,” said Hawley, the film’s costume designer.
Documentary Feature Film
- "The Alabama Solution"
- "Come See Me in the Good Light"
- "Cutting Through Rocks"
- "Mr. Nobody Against Putin"
- "The Perfect Neighbor"
“'Mr Nobody Against Putin' is about how you lose your country. And what we saw when working with this footage is that you lose it through countless small, little acts of complicity,” filmmaker David Borenstein said as he accepted the Oscar.
“We all face a moral choice, but luckily, even a nobody is more powerful than you think,” he said.
Documentary Short Film
- "All the Empty Rooms"
- "Armed Only with a Camera: The Life and Death of Brent Renaud"
- "Children No More: Were and Are Gone"
- "The Devil Is Busy"
- "Perfectly a Strangeness"
In this short directed by Joshua Seftel and produced by Conall Jones, journalist Steve Hartman and photographer Lou Bopp document the empty bedrooms of children killed in school shootings over the course of seven years.
Gloria Cazares, whose child was killed in the Uvalde school shooting, accepted the award.
“My daughter, Jackie, was nine years old when she was killed in Uvalde. Since that day, her bedroom has been frozen in time,” she said.
Discussing school shootings, Joshua Seftel told Spectrum News they [mass shootings] would be covered, focusing largely on the shooter, who the shooter was, and their backstory.
“The victims would often not even be talked about, or quickly be forgotten,” he told Spectrum News after winning the Academy Award. “That’s changing over time. It’s still something that we need to remember and focus on. With our film, what we tried to do was to completely focus on the children who are no longer here, because we think that by focusing on their lives and the loss and the absence of those children is what could help to change things and to move us toward finding more solutions.”
Seftel added that the U.S. has reached a point where school shootings are too common.
“There’s more than a 100 a year,” he said. “If we focus on the children who are gone, we’re more likely to remember these things that are fading so quickly from our minds.”
Film Editing
- "F1," Stephen Mirrione
- "Marty Supreme," Ronald Bronstein and Josh Safdie
- "One Battle After Another," Andy Jurgensen
- "Sentimental Value," Olivier Bugge Coutté
- "Sinners," Michael P. Shawver
"I want to give a special thank you to my editorial crew, who worked their butts off behind the scenes. You guys are amazing. Thank you to Paul. Thank you for taking me on this journey and our collaboration," said Jurgensen when he took the stage to accept his Oscar.
"I would like to dedicate this to my aunt, Barbara Hall, who was a film archivist for the Academy for over 25 years," he added.
Best International Feature Film
- "The Secret Agent" (Brazil)
- "It Was Just an Accident" (France)
- "Sentimental Value" (Norway)
- "Sirat" (Spain)
- "The Voice of Hind Rajab" (Tunisia)
"I'm just a film nerd from Norway. Thank you so much. Honestly, this means the world to me," said Joachim Trier as he accepted the Academy Award. "Thanks to the Academy. And thanks to Neon who brought our film over here, MK2, who helped us. This film is about a very dysfunctional family, and it's the opposite of what I felt with this beautiful group behind me. I think I make films to feel at home with people, and I've really felt at home with the crew."
Best Live Action Short Film
- "Butcher's Stain"
- "A Friend of Dorothy"
- "Jane Austen's Period Drama"
- "The Singers"
- "Two People Exchanging Saliva"
“Thank you to the Academy for supporting a movie that is weird, that is queer, and made by a majority of women!” said Natalie Musteata of “Two People Exchanging Saliva.”
Director Sam A. Davis of “Singers” called his short a “simple story about the power of music and art to bring us together in a moment when we live in an increasingly isolated world.”
Yes, there was a tie and it's not the first time this has happened at the Oscars.
The most recent tie came during the 2013 Oscars honoring films from 2012, when “Zero Dark Thirty” and “Skyfall” tied for the sound editing category. There have been five other ties in Oscars history, making Sunday’s tie the seventh.
The first tie, which was at the 5th Academy Awards almost 100 years ago, was based on an old rule. Wallace Beery (“The Champ”) and Fredric March (“Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde”) tied for best actor. They came within exactly one vote of each other, and in accordance with Academy rules at the time, they shared the recognition. That rule has since changed and only an exact match in totals would qualify as a tie today, according to the Academy.
Makeup and Hairstyling
- "Frankenstein"
- "Kokuho"
- "Sinners"
- "The Smashing Machine"
- "The Ugly Stepsister"
"While we’re making this film, we had the sense we’re part of something very special, and tonight confirms that,” makeup artist Mike Hill said as he accepted his Oscar.
Original Score
- "Bugonia," Jerskin Fendrix
- "Frankenstein," Alexandre Desplat
- "Hamnet," Max Richter
- "One Battle After Another," Jonny Greenwood
- "Sinners," Ludwig Goransson
“My dad bought his first blues album in Sweden, 1964,” Göransson said as he accepted his Academy Award.
“Even though it was on the other side of the world from a place my dad had never been, and a place he could not relate to, the music was so powerful it changed my dad’s life.”
Original Song
- "Dear Me" from "Diane Warren: Relentless"
- "Golden" from "KPop Demon Hunters"
- "I Lied To You" from "Sinners"
- "Sweet Dreams Of Joy" from "Viva Verdi!"
- "Train Dreams" from "Train Dreams"
"Growing up, you know, people made fun of me liking K-pop, but now everyone's singing our song and all the Korean lyrics. I'm so proud. And I realized, like the song, this award is not about success, it's about resilience," said EJAE during her Oscar acceptance speech.
Production Design
- "Frankenstein"
- "Hamnet"
- "Marty Supreme"
- "One Battle After Another"
- "Sinners"
"Guillermo, thank you for your humanity and your artistry. You are truly a master storyteller. It was an honor for us to help steer your fantastic operatic ship," said Tamara Deverell as she accepted her Oscar.
Sound
- "F1"
- "Frankenstein"
- "One Battle After Another"
- "Sinners"
- "Sirat"
"Our gratitude goes to our partners, our parents, our children, grandchildren. Movies are made for you. Go see the blockbusters. Go see the independents. Be inspired. Go with a friend, get a fresh point of view," said Gwendolyn Yates Whittle.
Visual Effects
- "Avatar: Fire and Ash"
- "F1"
- "Jurassic World Rebirth"
- "The Lost Bus"
- "Sinners"
Adapted Screenplay
- "Bugonia," Will Tracy
- "Frankenstein," Guillermo Del Toro
- "Hamnet," Chloé Zhao and Maggie O'Farrell
- "One Battle After Another," Paul Thomas Anderson
- "Train Dreams," Clint Bentley and Greg Kwedar
“I wrote this movie for my kids to say sorry for the housekeeping mess that we left in this world we’re handing off to them,” Anderson said as he accepted his Oscar.
"This is an adaptation, so I owe a huge debt of admiration and love to Thomas Pynchon. Any writer knows that...you either beg for forgiveness, or your special thanks is really to your family and the people that you share a roof with, who put up with what it means to live with a writer," he added.
Original Screenplay
- "Blue Moon," Robert Kaplow
- "It Was Just an Accident," Jafar Panahi
- "Marty Supreme," Ronald Bronstein and Josh Safdie
- "Sentimental Value," Eskil Vogt and Joachim Trier
- "Sinners," Ryan Coogler
During his speech, he asked the “Sinners” cast and crew to stand up. “You’re all winners in my book,” he said. "I want to thank the Academy for thinking of our movie that came out almost a year ago. This is an incredible honor. I want to thank my fellow nominees."
It has been another great year in filmmaking, and the only thing tighter than some of the Oscar races this year has been security for the 98th Academy Awards.
The unusually heavy security has been ramped up amid the ongoing Middle East war and concerns about retaliatory strikes by Iran. There have been no specific threats against the Oscars on Sunday, and last week, Gov. Gavin Newsom said the state has been working collaboratively with local law enforcement agencies and emergency services to ensure vital information is transmitted to keep communities safe.
The Los Angeles Police Department has set up a roughly one-mile security perimeter around the Dolby Theatre that includes uniformed officers, security cameras, K-9 units, and even surveillance drones.
In the end, all was calm, and all was bright for Hollywood’s biggest night.

sources.news_title: Paul Anthony Kelly Busts a Move at Armani's Pre-Oscars Party
sources.text:
Paul Anthony Kelly Busts a Move at Armani's Pre-Oscars Party
Paul Anthony Kelly Busting Moves at Armani Pre-Oscars Party!!!
Paul Anthony Kelly -- who plays John F. Kennedy Jr. in FX's limited series "Love Story: John F. Kennedy Jr. and Carolyn Bessette" -- looked like he was having a great time during Oscars weekend.
TMZ obtained video showing Kelly dancing at the Giorgio Armani pre-Oscars party in Los Angeles Saturday night.
In the video, Kelly is seen on a balcony area of the venue, moving to the music and chatting with people nearby as the star-studded event unfolds below.
The actor appears to be in a great mood, smiling and casually busting a few moves while enjoying the upbeat party atmosphere.
It appears the moment happened just before Kelly was scheduled to do an interview, but he clearly took a moment to soak up the party vibes first.
The star's recently premiered FX series explores the high-profile romance between the late political scion and the fashion publicist, Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy.
Their relationship captivated the public throughout the 1990s before the couple tragically died in a 1999 plane crash.
With the show already generating buzz, Kelly’s appearance at the Armani bash shows he’s settling comfortably into the spotlight -- and at least for Saturday night, he looked more than happy to celebrate with a little dancing before getting back to work.

It’s ‘Sinners’ v ‘One Battle’ as Oscars day arrives
Both frontrunner films have a chance of breaking the all-time Oscar wins record
After months of expensive campaigns, the Oscars finally arrive today, with all eyes on the race between One Battle After Another and Sinners for best picture, Hollywood’s most coveted prize.
Ahead of the star-packed gala, pundits say the Leonardo DiCaprio-starring political thriller One Battle is neck-and-neck with Michael B. Jordan’s bluesy vampire horror Sinners, while several acting prizes are similarly impossible to call.
Read the full story on Times2.

sources.news_title: Top Oscars 2026 nominated movies you can watch in India
sources.text:
Hyderabad: As the 98th Academy Awards approach, film lovers in India are catching up on the nominated movies before the ceremony. Many of these films are now available on streaming platforms, while some are still running in theatres across the country.
Oscar 2026 Movies Available on OTT Platforms
Several Oscar-nominated films can be watched online on popular streaming platforms.
Sinners
A supernatural thriller directed by Ryan Coogler and starring Michael B. Jordan in a double role as twin brothers who return to their hometown and confront a dark force.
One Battle After Another
Directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, the action drama stars Leonardo DiCaprio as a former revolutionary forced to return to his dangerous past to protect his daughter.
Frankenstein
Guillermo del Toro’s gothic science fiction drama based on Mary Shelley’s classic novel. The film stars Oscar Isaac as Victor Frankenstein and Jacob Elordi as the creature.
Marty Supreme
A sports comedy drama starring Timothée Chalamet as a table tennis player inspired by real-life champion Marty Reisman.
Hamnet
Directed by Chloé Zhao, the historical drama explores the emotional story of William Shakespeare and his wife coping with the loss of their son.
F1 The Movie
A sports drama starring Brad Pitt as a veteran Formula One driver who returns to the racing world to mentor a young driver.
Bugonia
A sci-fi thriller directed by Yorgos Lanthimos. The story follows two men who kidnap a powerful CEO because they believe she is an alien.
The Secret Agent
A historical political thriller starring Wagner Moura, set during the Brazilian military dictatorship.
Train Dreams
A quiet drama about a railroad worker navigating grief and massive social change in early twentieth-century America.
Sentimental Value
An emotional drama about two sisters reconnecting with their estranged father after their mother’s death.
These ten films are competing for the Best Picture award at the Oscars 2026, which will be held on March 15, 2026 in Los Angeles and will be streamed in India early morning on March 16.
Oscars 2026 Telecast in India
The 98th Academy Awards will take place on March 15, 2026 at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles. Due to the time difference, Indian audiences can watch the ceremony early on March 16.
The red carpet coverage will begin at 4:30 AM IST, and the main awards ceremony will start at around 5:30 AM IST. Viewers in India can watch the event live on JioHotstar.

sources.news_title: 'One Battle After Another' Big Winner at the Oscars, Chalamet Goes Home without an Award.
sources.text:
De Oscaravond eindigt in een spannende tweestrijd tussen 'One battle after another' en 'Sinners', maar uiteindelijk trekt de eerstgenoemde met 6 Oscars aan het langste eind. De film wint zowel Beste Regie als Beste Film, 2 van de meest prestigieuze prijzen van de avond. Sinners (4 Oscars) blijft niet met lege handen achter: de film wint Beste Cinematografie en Beste Acteur in een Hoofdrol. Opvallend: Sean Penn, die de Oscar voor Beste Acteur in een Bijrol heeft gewonnen voor 'One battle after another', kwam niet opdagen.
'One battle after another' grote winnaar op de Oscars, Chalamet zonder prijs naar huis
Aan het begin van de avond leek 'One battle after another' op weg naar een duidelijke overwinning. De film stapelde de vroege Oscars op en leek even ongenaakbaar. Maar toen 'Sinners' onverwacht Beste Cinematografie won, kantelde de sfeer.
De spanning steeg nog verder toen Michael B. Jordan de Oscar voor Beste Acteur in een Hoofdrol binnenhaalde. Precies zoals voorspeld werd: de race tussen de 2 films zou pas helemaal op het einde beslist worden.
En zo geschiedde. Pas bij de allerlaatste categorie werd de doorslag gegeven. 'One battle after another' mocht Beste Film in ontvangst nemen en kroonde zich daarmee tot de uitgesproken winnaar van de avond. De eindstand: 'One battle after another' kon 6 van de 13 nominaties verzilveren. 'Sinners' won er 4 van de (historische) 16.
'One Battle after Another' versus 'Sinners'
'One Battle after Another' won de Oscar voor:
Beste Film
Beste Regisseur (Paul Thomas Anderson)
Beste Aangepaste Script
Beste Acteur in een Bijrol (Sean Penn)
Beste Casting
Beste Montage
'Sinners' won de Oscar voor:
Beste Acteur in een Hoofdrol (Michael B. Jordan)
Beste Cinematografie
Beste Originele Script
Beste Muziek
Voor 'Marty supreme', met Timothée Chalamet in de hoofdrol, bleef het bij nominaties: de film gaat uiteindelijk met lege handen naar huis. 'Frankenstein' kan met 3 Oscars dan wel weer tevreden terugkijken op de 98e editie van de Oscars.
2 uitslagen waren dan weer totaal geen verrassing: Jessie Buckley won overtuigend de Oscar voor Beste Actrice in een Hoofdrol, en 'Golden' (dat ene nummer uit 'KPop demon hunters' dat al maanden in je hoofd zit) werd bekroond tot Beste Nummer.
Beste film
‘One battle after another’ gaat niet alleen met de meeste Oscars naar huis, maar sleepte ook de hoofdprijs in de wacht. Dat was vooraf geen uitgemaakte zaak: de film moest het opnemen tegen het recordgenomineerde 'Sinners'. Tijdens het volledige awardseizoen gingen de 2 films nek aan nek, waarbij de ene film de ene prijs won en de andere vervolgens weer terrein terugpakte.
Toch trok 'One battle after another' in de beslissende momenten aan het langste eind. "Wat een avond, mensen", zegt regisseur Paul Thomas Anderson in de wolken. "Laat ons een martini drinken. Dit is echt ongelooflijk. Proost. Heel erg bedankt."
'One battle after another', ook van filmstudio Warner Bros., is een satirische actiekomedie over een groep ex-revolutionairen die weer bij elkaar komt als hun vijand na lange tijd weer opduikt. De hoofdrol is voor Leonardo DiCaprio, die als uitgebluste en paranoïde ex-revolutionair Bob zijn dochter moet proberen te redden en tegelijk zijn verleden onder ogen moet zien.
Beste acteur hoofdrol
Michael B. Jordan heeft de Oscar voor Beste Acteur in een Hoofdrol gewonnen. De 39‑jarige acteur was dit jaar voor het eerst genomineerd en won eerder al een Actors Award, een belangrijke indicator binnen het prijzencircuit.
Jordan leek in shock toen zijn naam weerklonk. Met zijn overwinning klopt hij de andere favorieten, Timothée Chalamet in 'Marty Supreme' en Leonardo DiCaprio in 'One battle after another'.
'Sinners', een film uit de stal van Warner Bros. en geregisseerd door Ryan Coogler, speelt zich af in de jaren 30 in het zuiden van de Verenigde Staten. Tweelingbroers Smoke en Stack (allebei gespeeld door Jordan) keren vanuit Chicago terug naar hun geboortestad om er een muziekbar voor zwarten te openen. Op de openingsavond duiken echter witte vampiers op. Wat volgt is een groot muzikaal én bloederig festijn.
Jordans overwinning werd ontvangen met luid applaus en een staande ovatie. Dat de zaal hem de Oscar gunde, moge wel duidelijk zijn.
Jordan is de zesde zwarte man die de Oscar voor Beste Acteur ontvangt. En dat beseft hij maar al te goed. "Ik sta hier dankzij de mensen die mij zijn voorgegaan,” zegt hij zichtbaar overweldigd. Daarop noemde hij alle zwarte mannen die het beeldje al in ontvangst hebben mogen nemen in deze categorie, onder wie Will Smith en Jamie Foxx.
Jordan nam ook de tijd om zijn fans te bedanken. "Dank jullie wel dat jullie in mij blijven geloven. Ik weet dat jullie willen dat ik het goed doe. En ik wil dat ook, omdat jullie op mij hebben ingezet. En ik zal blijven opstaan."
Beste actrice hoofdrol
Jessie Buckley heeft haar eerste Oscar gewonnen, een mijlpaal in de carrière van de Ierse actrice en zangeres. De 36‑jarige Buckley gold vooraf als de uitgesproken favoriete en bevestigt dat met deze overwinning. Het is haar tweede Oscarnominatie, na 'The lost daughter' in 2021.
Ze werd bekroond voor haar rol in 'Hamnet', waarin ze Agnes vertolkt, de echtgenote van William Shakespeare en moeder van titelfiguur Hamnet.
Op het podium kon ze haar emoties nauwelijks bedwingen. Buckley wisselde tussen lachen en tranen terwijl ze haar beeldje omklemde. Ze richtte zich eerst tot de andere genomineerden, die ze omschreef als buitengewone vrouwen met wie ze zich vereerd voelde het podium te delen.
Daarna sprak ze liefdevol over haar ouders, die haar leerden "groot te dromen" en haar aanmoedigden haar eigen pad te volgen. Ook haar man, Freddie Sorensen, kreeg een warme ode: haar beste vriend, een fantastische vader, en iemand met wie ze gerust "nog 20.000 kinderen" zou willen krijgen, grapte ze.
Hun dochtertje Isla, amper 8 maanden oud, lag volgens Buckley waarschijnlijk ergens te slapen, totaal onbewust van het moment, "waarschijnlijk dromend over melk".
Beste acteur bijrol
Sean Penn heeft de Oscar voor Beste Mannelijke Bijrol gewonnen voor zijn rol als kolonel Lockjaw in 'One battle after another'. Het is zijn derde Oscar, na eerdere overwinningen voor 'Mystic river' en 'Milk'.
Opvallend: Penn was niet aanwezig in de zaal om de prijs in ontvangst te nemen. Later dezelfde dag dook hij op in de Oekraïense hoofdstad Kiev.
Omdat Penn er niet was, nam Kieran Culkin - de winnaar van vorig jaar in dezelfde categorie - de Oscar in zijn plaats in ontvangst.
Beste actrice bijrol
Amy Madigan heeft op 75‑jarige leeftijd de Oscar voor Beste Vrouwelijke Bijrol gewonnen. Ze won eerder begin maart al een Actors Award. Madigan behaalde voor horrorfilm 'Weapons' de enige Oscarnominatie van de film.
Het is haar tweede Oscarnominatie. Haar eerste dateert van 1986 voor 'Twice in a lifetime' (profetische titel!). Er zit dus exact 40 jaar tussen beide nominaties. "Maar deze keer win ik het gouden beeldje", zegt Madigan, duidelijk opgetogen nadat ze eerst hartelijk lachend het podium betrad.
"Dit is geweldig. Gisteren, terwijl ik mijn benen aan het scheren was in de douche, was ik aan het nadenken over wat ik zou zeggen als ik zou winnen. Ik draag een broek vandaag, dus ik had me er niet druk over moeten maken", zegt ze geamuseerd. "Heel erg bedankt, ik ben enorm overweldigd."
Madigan beleeft de voorbije periode een duidelijke carrièreheropleving dankzij haar rol als Aunt Gladys in 'Weapons'. De film, geregisseerd door Zach Cregger, draait rond een kleine gemeenschap waar 17 kinderen midden in de nacht hun huis verlaten en verdwijnen.
Beste film internationaal
'Sentimental value', van de Noorse regisseur Joachim Trier, heeft de Oscar voor Beste Internationale Film gewonnen. De Zweedse veteraan Stellan Skarsgård speelt in de film misschien wel de rol van zijn leven als Gustav, een gelauwerde filmregisseur die na de dood van zijn echtgenote terugkeert naar het ouderlijk huis in Oslo. Zijn 2 dochters staan niet bepaald klaar om hem met open armen te ontvangen, want tijdens zijn carrière blonk hij vooral uit in afwezigheid.
"Deze film gaat over een heel disfunctionele familie, het tegenovergestelde van de ploeg met wie ik de film heb mogen maken", zegt Trier. "Ik denk dat ik films maak om me thuis te voelen bij mensen. Er hebben 1.072 mensen meegewerkt aan deze film. Ik hou van hen allemaal."
'Sentimental value' wordt al lang getipt als een van de meest emotioneel geladen titels van het seizoen en verzilvert daarmee zijn status als publieksfavoriet.
Beste regisseur
Na 14 nominaties heeft Paul Thomas Anderson eindelijk zijn eerste Oscars gewonnen. Meervoud, want hij won niet alleen als regisseur, maar ook als producer en scenarist.
“Jullie hebben me hard doen werken voor deze Oscar", zegt hij lachend. "Ik sta hier dankzij het vertrouwen en de tijd die mensen in mij hebben gestoken. Er zal altijd een beetje twijfel blijven of je het wel verdient, maar het plezier om het beeld zelf vast te houden staat buiten kijf."
Beste animatiefilm
'KPop demon hunters', een film over een vrouwelijk K‑poptrio dat de wereld moet redden van kwaadaardige krachten, is uitgegroeid tot een wereldwijd fenomeen.
"Bedankt aan alle fans", zegt Maggie Kang, een van de 3 makers, zichtbaar emotioneel. "Aan iedereen die eruitziet zoals ik: het spijt me dat het zo lang heeft geduurd voor we iemand als wij in een film als deze zien. Maar hier zijn we. Deze Oscar is voor Korea en Koreanen overal."
Sinds de release op Netflix in juni werd de film in twee weken tijd 33 miljoen keer bekeken. De film haalde ook de top 10 van de Netflix‑ranglijsten in 93 landen. En of je de film hebt gezien of niet: 'Golden', het nummer uit de film, heb je ongetwijfeld al (te?) vaak gehoord. Dat nummer is trouwens ook genomineerd voor een Oscar.
Voor de fans is er goed nieuws, want vorige week raakte bekend dat er een sequel komt.
Beste originele nummer
De Oscar voor Beste Nummer gaat dit jaar naar ‘Golden’ uit 'KPop demon hunters', een overwinning die al even in de lucht hing, maar toch voor een uitgelaten reactie in de zaal zorgde. Het is - na Beste Animatiefilm - de tweede win voor de film. 'Golden' groeide de voorbije maanden uit tot een wereldwijd fenomeen. Het nummer werd intussen 1,48 miljard keer beluisterd op Spotify.
Beste documentaire
'Mr. Nobody against Putin' heeft Beste Documentaire gewonnen. Een opvallende, maar niet geheel onverwachte bekroning voor een documentaire die internationaal veel stof deed opwaaien.
"De documentaire gaat over hoe je je land verliest", zegt maker David Borenstein. "We hebben, tijdens het maken van 'Mr. Nobody against Putin', gezien dat dat gebeurt door talloze daden van medeplichtigheid: als je ziet dat je overheid mensen vermoordt op straat en niets doet, als je niets zegt wanneer oligarchen de media overnemen."
'Mr. Nobody against Putin' is overigens te zien op VRT MAX .
Beste korte animatiefilm
'The girl who cried pearls' is een Canadese stop-motion-kortfilm over een jongen die verliefd wordt op een meisje dat ’s nachts parels huilt. "Mensen denken dat het veel geduld vraagt om 5 jaar lang een poppenfilm te maken. Maar eigenlijk vraagt het veel meer geduld om 5 jaar samen te wonen met iemand die een poppenfilm maakt, dus heel veel dank aan mijn vrouw", zegt maker Chris Lavis.

sources.news_title: ‘Sinners’ and ‘One Battle After Another’ poised for an all-Warner Bros. showdown at Academy Awards - The Boston Globe
sources.text:
NEW YORK (AP) — Hollywood will convene Sunday night for a nail-biter Academy Awards that’s steering toward a coronation for either Paul Thomas Anderson or Ryan Coogler. Most would call that a win-win.
Anderson’s “One Battle After Another” is the favorite heading into the ceremony at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles. But Coogler’s “Sinners” comes in the lead nominee with a record 16 nominations. Both filmmakers are poised to leave with their first Oscar.
But little else is assured at an Academy Awards where Michael B. Jordan or Timothée Chalamet (despite the ballet diss heard ‘round the world) could win their first Academy Award in a too-close-to-call best actor race.
How to watch and stream the Oscars and red carpet
The telecast will air live on ABC and stream on Hulu beginning at 7 p.m. Eastern. (YouTube will be the new home of the Oscars beginning in 2029.) The official red carpet preshow begins on ABC and Hulu at 6:30 p.m. EDT, while E! will kick off its red-carpet broadcast at 4 p.m.
The Associated Press will have a livestream of fashion arrivals from noon to 3:30 p.m. Pacific on APNews.com and YouTube.
FEATURED VIDEO
What to expect from the 2026 Oscars
Conan O’Brien is returning as host for the second year in a row. Despite the war in Iran and expanding geopolitical turmoil, O’Brien has pledged an entertaining show in the mold of hosts like Bob Hope and Johnny Carson. “Let’s have fun with it, is my attitude,” O’Brien told reporters earlier in the week.
Still, the already high security will be even greater this year at an Oscars, taking place two weeks after the United States and President Donald Trump launched the war with Iran.
“Of course, every year we monitor what’s going on in the world,” Raj Kapoor, executive producer of the show, said earlier in the week. “We have the support of the FBI and the LAPD, and it’s a close collaboration.”
Two of the five best song nominees will be performed: “I Lied to You,” from “Sinners,” with Miles Caton, Raphael Saadiq and others; and “Golden” from “KPop Demon Hunters.”
Advertisement
Theatrical looks to best streaming, again
“KPop Demon Hunters,” a Sony Pictures production that was sold to Netflix, was the most-watched movie of 2025. (It has 325 million views and counting, making it Netflix’s most-streamed movie ever.) But it seems all but certain that the night’s final award won’t go to a streaming release; Apple’s “CODA” remains the only to achieve that. Instead best picture is likely to go to an anomaly in today’s movie industry: big-budget original films from a personal vision.
“Sinners” and “One Battle After Another” were both theatrical releases shot on film. And both came from Warner Bros., the legacy studio that’s agreed to merge with David Ellison’s new media colossus, Paramount Skydance. The $111 billion deal, which awaits regulatory approval, has rattled an industry already reconciling itself to the acquisitions of MGM (by Amazon) and 20th Century Fox (by The Walt Disney Co.).
Elegy may mark Sunday’s Oscars. The in memoriam segment is expected to include, among many others, remembrances of Robert Redford, Diane Keaton and Robert Duvall. O’Brien, who had hosted a party attended by Rob and Michele Reiner the night before their deaths, has promised a “very powerful” tribute.
New this year is a best casting category. Another innovation is a requirement that Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences members watch all nominees before voting. On the academy’s streaming platform — even Oscar voting is streamed — voters had to check a box attesting to having watched each nominee before voting in a category.
Few sure things in the acting categories
Whether those changes will have any effect on some of the night’s closest races remains to be seen. Coming into the show, best actor is one of the most hard-to-call categories. Chalamet had been seen as the front-runner for his performance in “Marty Supreme.” But a swaggering meta campaign, that drew headlines, of all things, a perceived slight of ballet and opera, may have helped put Jordan into the lead. (In Chalamet’s favor, the uproar only started as voting was ending.)
Advertisement
While Jessie Buckley (“Hamnet”) is widely expecting to win best actress, a first for Irish performers, the supporting categories are highly competitive. Amy Madigan (“Weapons”) is the slight favorite in best supporting actress, but Teyana Taylor (“One Battle After Another”) and Wunmi Mosaku (“Sinners”) are in the mix, too.
Despite almost no campaigning, Penn is viewed as the best supporting actor favorite. That award, could easily also go to Stellan Skarsgård (“Sentimental Value”) or Delroy Lindo (“Sinners”).
Though the Oscars often feel largely removed from their times, a crop of nominees that explicitly grapple with the current political moment will be center stage. That includes not just “One Battle After Another,” which opens with a raid on an immigration detention facility, but movies like Kleber Mendonça Filho’s Brazilian political thriller “The Secret Agent” and Jafar Panahi’s Iranian revenge drama “It Was Just an Accident.”
The war in Iran has particular meaning to Panahi, whose film is nominated for best international feature and for best screenplay. The esteemed Iranian filmmaker and last year’s Palme d’Or winner has made films clandestinely in his native Iran despite repeated imprisonment, travel ban and even home arrest. While promoting the film, Panahi was sentenced to a year in prison. At least one of his cowriter nominees, Mehdi Mahmoudian, was unable to leave Iran to attend Sunday’s awards.
Twenty three years ago, the Academy Awards were also held amid war in the Middle East. The 2003 Oscars took place just three days before the Iraq War began. Many in Hollywood protested the war. “Chicago” won best picture.

sources.news_title: 'One Battle After Another' wins best picture at 98th Academy Awards
sources.text:
‘One Battle After Another’ triumphs at 98th Academy Awards in coronation for Paul Thomas Anderson
‘One Battle After Another’ triumphs at 98th Academy Awards in coronation for Paul Thomas Anderson
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Paul Thomas Anderson’s “One Battle After Another” was crowned best picture at the 98th Academy Awards, handing Hollywood’s top honor to a comic, multi-generational American saga of political resistance.
The ceremony Sunday, which also saw Michael B. Jordan win best actor and “Sinners” cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw make Oscar history as the first female director of photography to win the award, was a long-in-coming coronation for Anderson, a San Fernando Valley native who made his first short at age 18 and has been one of America’s most lionized filmmakers for decades. Before Sunday, Anderson had never won an Oscar.
But “One Battle After Another,” the favorite coming in, won six Oscars, including best director and best adapted screenplay for Anderson, the Oscars’ first trophy for best casting and best supporting actor for an absent Sean Penn.
“I wrote this movie for my kids to say sorry for the housekeeping mess that we left in this world — we’re handing off to them,” said Anderson while accepting the screenplay trophy. “But also with the encouragement that they will be the generation that hopefully brings us some common sense and decency.”
Ryan Coogler’s Jim Crow-set, blues-soaked vampire tale “Sinners,” which came in with a record 16 nominations, also landed some big and even historic wins. Coogler, the widely loved filmmaker, won the first Oscar in an unblemished career that started out with Jordan in 2013’s “Fruitvale Station.”
Arkapaw was also the first Black person to win for best cinematography. Only the fourth female cinematographer ever nominated, her win was a long-in-coming triumph for women behind the camera.
“I really want all the women in room to stand up,” said Arkapaw. “Because I don’t feel like I get here without you guys.”
And Jordan, one of Hollywood’s most liked leading men, won best actor in one of the night’s closest races. The Dolby Theatre rose to its feet in the most thunderous applause of the night.
“Yo, momma, what’s up?” said Jordan after staggering to the stage.
The Oscar night belonged to Warner Bros., the studio of “One Battle After Another” and “Sinners,” which scored a record-tying 11 wins. It was an oddly poignant note of triumph for the fabled studio, which weeks earlier agreed to a sale to Paramount Skydance, David Ellison’s rapidly assembled media monolith. The $111 billion deal, which awaits regulatory approval, has Hollywood bracing for more layoffs.
But “Sinners” and “One Battle After Another” — the much-acclaimed heavyweights of the season — were each Hollywood anomalies: big-budget originals born from a personal vision. In a year where anxiety over studio contraction and the rise of artificial intelligence often consumed the industry, both films gave Hollywood fresh hope.
Jessie Buckley won best actress for her performance as Agnes Shakespeare in “Hamnet,” making her the first Irish performer to ever win in the category. At an Oscars where no other acting award seemed a sure thing, Buckley cruised into Sunday’s Oscars at the Dolby Theatre as the overwhelming favorite.
“It’s Mother’s Day in the U.K.,” said Buckley on the stage. “I would like to dedicated this to the beautiful chaos of a mother’s heart.”
‘KPop’ and ‘Frankenstein’ win for Netflix
From the start, when host Conan O’Brien sprinted through the year’s nominees as Amy Madigan’s character in the horror thriller “Weapons” in a pre-taped bit, Sunday’s ceremony was quirky, a little clunky and preoccupied with the shifting place of movies in culture. There was, of all things, a tie for best live-action short film.
As expected, the Netflix sensation “KPop Demon Hunters,” 2025’s most-watched film, won best animated feature, as well as best song for “Golden.” It was a big win for Netflix but a more qualified victory for the movie’s producer, Sony Pictures. Though it developed and produced the film, Sony sold “KPop Demon Hunters” to the streaming giant instead of giving it a theatrical release.
On Netflix, “KPop Demon Hunters” became a cultural phenomenon and the streaming platform’s biggest hit. It has more than 325 million views and counting.
“This is for Korea and Koreans everywhere,” said co-director Maggie Kang.
Another Netflix release, Guillermo del Toro’s “Frankenstein” picked up three awards for its lavish craft, for costume design, makeup and hairstyling and for production design.
Amy Madigan won best supporting actress for her performance in the horror thriller “Weapons,” a win that came 40 years after the 75-year-old actor was first nominated, in 1986, for “Twice in a Lifetime.” Letting out a giant laugh as she hit the stage, Madigan exclaimed, “This is great!”
O’Brien presides over a ceremony shadowed by politics
Hosting for the second time, O’Brien began the Dolby Theatre show alluding to “chaotic and frightening times.” But he argued that the current geopolitical climate made the Oscars all the more resonate as a globally unifying force.
“We pay tribute tonight, not just to film, but to the ideals of global artistry, collaboration, patience, resilience and that rarest of qualities today — optimism,” O’Brien said. “We’re going to celebrate. Not because we think all is well, but because we work, and hope, for better.”
Throughout the show, O’Brien hit a number of targets, like Timothée Chalamet — who again missed out on winning his first Oscar, this time for “Marty Supreme” — for his diss of opera and ballet. But the ceremony seldom wasn’t shadowed by politics, whether in references to changes under U.S. President Donald Trump or the recently launched war in Iran.
Joachim Trier, whose Norwegian family drama “Sentimental Value” won best international film, quoted James Baldwin in his acceptance speech: “All adults are responsible for all children,” he said. “Let’s not vote for politicians that don’t take this seriously into account.”
Presenter Jimmy Kimmel, whose late-night show last year was suspended after comments he made about Charlie Kirk’s killing, was among the most blunt.
“There are some countries that don’t support free speech,” said Kimmel. “I’m not at liberty to say which. Let’s just leave it at North Korea and CBS.”
Shortly after, “Mr. Nobody Against Putin,” a film about a Russian primary schoolteacher who documents his students’ indoctrination to support Russia’s war with Ukraine, won best documentary.
“‘Mr. Nobody Against Putin’ is about how you lose your country,” co-director said. “And what we saw when working with this footage is that you lose it through countless, small, little acts of complicity.”
“We all face a moral choice,” he added, “but, luckily, a nobody is more powerful than you think.”
Tributes to Reiner, Redford and others
Elegy also marked the Oscars. Producers expanded the in memoriam segment following a year that featured the deaths of so many Hollywood legends, including Keaton, Robert Duvall and Redford. Barbra Streisand spoke about Redford, her “The Way We Were” co-star.
“Bob had real backbone,” said Streisand, who called Redford “an intellectual cowboy” before singing a few bars of “The Way We Were.”
Billy Crystal paid tribute to Rob and Michele Reiner, who were killed in their home in December. Crystal, a close friend of Rob Reiner’s who memorably starred in 1989’s “When Harry Met Sally...” and 1987’s “Princess Bride.” In his moving remarks, Crystal quoted the latter.
“All we can say is: Buddy, how much fun we had storming the castle,” said Crystal.
Theatrical bests streaming, again
Yet again, the night’s final award again didn’t go to a streaming release; Apple’s “CODA” remains the only streaming film to achieve that distinction. “Sinners” and “One Battle After Another” were both theatrical releases shot on film.
Apple’s top contender this time, the Formula One race drama “F1,” a movie that it partnered with Warner Bros. to distribute theatrically, won for best sound. The lone blockbuster of the year to go home with a win was “Avatar: Fire and Ash,” for visual effects.
Some of O’Brien’s best digs came at the expense of the streamers. Netflix chief Ted Sarandos, he joked, was in a theater for the first time. The host also lamented the lack of nominees for Amazon MGM: “Why isn’t the website I order toilet paper from winning more Oscars?”
“I’m honored to be the last human host of the Academy Awards,” said O’Brien. “Next year it’s going to be a Waymo in a tux.”

sources.news_title: Michael B. Jordan wins best actor Oscar, Paul Thomas Anderson wins best director
sources.text:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Paul Thomas Anderson’s “One Battle After Another” was crowned best picture at the 98th Academy Awards, handing Hollywood’s top honor to a comic, multi-generational American saga of political resistance.
The ceremony Sunday, which also saw Michael B. Jordan win best actor and “Sinners” cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw make Oscar history as the first female director of photography to win the award, was a long-in-coming coronation for Anderson, a San Fernando Valley native who made his first short at age 18 and has been one of America’s most lionized filmmakers for decades. Before Sunday, Anderson had never won an Oscar.
But “One Battle After Another,” the favorite coming in, won six Oscars, including best director and best adapted screenplay for Anderson, the Oscars' first trophy for best casting and best supporting actor for an absent Sean Penn.
“I wrote this movie for my kids to say sorry for the housekeeping mess that we left in this world — we’re handing off to them,” said Anderson while accepting the screenplay trophy. “But also with the encouragement that they will be the generation that hopefully brings us some common sense and decency.”
Ryan Coogler's Jim Crow-set, blues-soaked vampire tale “Sinners,” which came in with a record 16 nominations, also landed some big and even historic wins. Coogler, the widely loved filmmaker, won the first Oscar in an unblemished career that started out with Jordan in 2013's “Fruitvale Station.”
Arkapaw was also the first Black person to win for best cinematography. Only the fourth female cinematographer ever nominated, her win was a long-in-coming triumph for women behind the camera.
“I really want all the women in room to stand up,” said Arkapaw. “Because I don’t feel like I get here without you guys.”
And Jordan, one of Hollywood's most liked leading men, won best actor in one of the night's closest races. The Dolby Theatre rose to its feet in the most thunderous applause of the night.
“Yo, momma, what’s up?” said Jordan after staggering to the stage.
The Oscar night belonged to Warner Bros., the studio of “One Battle After Another” and “Sinners,” which scored a record-tying 11 wins. It was an oddly poignant note of triumph for the fabled studio, which weeks earlier agreed to a sale to Paramount Skydance, David Ellison’s rapidly assembled media monolith. The $111 billion deal, which awaits regulatory approval, has Hollywood bracing for more layoffs.
But “Sinners” and “One Battle After Another” — the much-acclaimed heavyweights of the season — were each Hollywood anomalies: big-budget originals born from a personal vision. In a year where anxiety over studio contraction and the rise of artificial intelligence often consumed the industry, both films gave Hollywood fresh hope.
Jessie Buckley won best actress for her performance as Agnes Shakespeare in “Hamnet,” making her the first Irish performer to ever win in the category. At an Oscars where no other acting award seemed a sure thing, Buckley cruised into Sunday’s Oscars at the Dolby Theatre as the overwhelming favorite.
“It's Mother's Day in the U.K.,” said Buckley on the stage. “I would like to dedicated this to the beautiful chaos of a mother's heart.”
‘KPop’ and ‘Frankenstein’ win for Netflix
From the start, when host Conan O'Brien sprinted through the year's nominees as Amy Madigan's character in the horror thriller “Weapons” in a pre-taped bit, Sunday's ceremony was quirky, a little clunky and preoccupied with the shifting place of movies in culture. There was, of all things, a tie for best live-action short film.
As expected, the Netflix sensation “KPop Demon Hunters,” 2025’s most-watched film, won best animated feature, as well as best song for “Golden.” It was a big win for Netflix but a more qualified victory for the movie’s producer, Sony Pictures. Though it developed and produced the film, Sony sold “KPop Demon Hunters” to the streaming giant instead of giving it a theatrical release.
On Netflix, “KPop Demon Hunters” became a cultural phenomenon and the streaming platform’s biggest hit. It has more than 325 million views and counting.
“This is for Korea and Koreans everywhere,” said co-director Maggie Kang.
Another Netflix release, Guillermo del Toro’s “Frankenstein” picked up three awards for its lavish craft, for costume design, makeup and hairstyling and for production design.
Amy Madigan won best supporting actress for her performance in the horror thriller “Weapons,” a win that came 40 years after the 75-year-old actor was first nominated, in 1986, for “Twice in a Lifetime.” Letting out a giant laugh as she hit the stage, Madigan exclaimed, “This is great!”
O'Brien presides over a ceremony shadowed by politics
Hosting for the second time, O'Brien began the Dolby Theatre show alluding to “chaotic and frightening times.” But he argued that the current geopolitical climate made the Oscars all the more resonate as a globally unifying force.
“We pay tribute tonight, not just to film, but to the ideals of global artistry, collaboration, patience, resilience and that rarest of qualities today — optimism,” O'Brien said. “We’re going to celebrate. Not because we think all is well, but because we work, and hope, for better.”
Throughout the show, O'Brien hit a number of targets, like Timothée Chalamet — who again missed out on winning his first Oscar, this time for “Marty Supreme” — for his diss of opera and ballet. But the ceremony seldom wasn't shadowed by politics, whether in references to changes under U.S. President Donald Trump or the recently launched war in Iran.
Joachim Trier, whose Norwegian family drama “Sentimental Value” won best international film, quoted James Baldwin in his acceptance speech: “All adults are responsible for all children,” he said. “Let’s not vote for politicians that don’t take this seriously into account.”
Presenter Jimmy Kimmel, whose late-night show last year was suspended after comments he made about Charlie Kirk's killing, was among the most blunt.
“There are some countries that don’t support free speech,” said Kimmel. “I’m not at liberty to say which. Let’s just leave it at North Korea and CBS.”
Shortly after, “Mr. Nobody Against Putin,” a film about a Russian primary schoolteacher who documents his students' indoctrination to support Russia's war with Ukraine, won best documentary.
“'Mr. Nobody Against Putin' is about how you lose your country,” co-director said. “And what we saw when working with this footage is that you lose it through countless, small, little acts of complicity.”
“We all face a moral choice,” he added, “but, luckily, a nobody is more powerful than you think.”
Tributes to Reiner, Redford and others
Elegy also marked the Oscars. Producers expanded the in memoriam segment following a year that featured the deaths of so many Hollywood legends, including Keaton, Robert Duvall and Redford. Barbra Streisand spoke about Redford, her “The Way We Were” co-star.
“Bob had real backbone,” said Streisand, who called Redford “an intellectual cowboy” before singing a few bars of “The Way We Were.”
Billy Crystal paid tribute to Rob and Michele Reiner, who were killed in their home in December. Crystal, a close friend of Rob Reiner's who memorably starred in 1989's “When Harry Met Sally...” and 1987's “Princess Bride.” In his moving remarks, Crystal quoted the latter.
“All we can say is: Buddy, how much fun we had storming the castle,” said Crystal.
Theatrical bests streaming, again
Yet again, the night’s final award again didn't go to a streaming release; Apple's “CODA” remains the only streaming film to achieve that distinction. “Sinners” and “One Battle After Another” were both theatrical releases shot on film.
Apple's top contender this time, the Formula One race drama “F1,” a movie that it partnered with Warner Bros. to distribute theatrically, won for best sound. The lone blockbuster of the year to go home with a win was “Avatar: Fire and Ash,” for visual effects.
Some of O’Brien’s best digs came at the expense of the streamers. Netflix chief Ted Sarandos, he joked, was in a theater for the first time. The host also lamented the lack of nominees for Amazon MGM: “Why isn’t the website I order toilet paper from winning more Oscars?”
“I’m honored to be the last human host of the Academy Awards,” said O’Brien. “Next year it’s going to be a Waymo in a tux.”
___

sources.news_title: Everything You Need to Know About the Oscars
sources.text:
Tout ce qu’il faut savoir en vue des Oscars
Un duel historique se dessine entre Sinners et Une bataille après l'autre, en compétition dans 11 catégories.
Photo : the academy via getty images / Getty
Un duel historique se dessine en vue de la 98e cérémonie des Oscars dimanche soir puisque Sinners et Une bataille après l’autre s’affrontent dans un nombre record de 11 catégories, du jamais-vu depuis la création de ces prix, en 1929. Des grands favoris aux prestations musicales attendues, voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir en vue de la grand-messe du cinéma hollywoodien.
Avec 16 nominations, un autre record historique, Sinners – film d’horreur mâtiné de blues signé Ryan Coogler – mène le bal avec des mentions notamment pour les prix du meilleur film, du meilleur réalisateur, du meilleur acteur et du meilleur scénario original.
Une bataille après l’autre, une tragicomédie de Paul Thomas Anderson sur les dérives extrémistes des États-Unis, suit juste derrière avec 13 nominations.
Le Frankenstein de Guillermo Del Toro est en lice pour neuf Oscars, tout comme Valeur sentimentale de Joachim Trier et Marty Supreme de Josh Safdie. Le film Hamnet de Chloe Zhao a de son côté récolté huit nominations.
Dans Une bataille après l'autre, Leonardo DiCaprio incarne Bob Ferguson, un ancien révolutionnaire désabusé dont la fille a été kidnappée.
Photo : Warner Bros. Pictures
Qui remportera l’Oscar du meilleur film?
De Variety au Hollywood Reporter en passant par l’Associated Press, Deadline et le New York Times, la majorité des médias prédisent que l’un ou l’autre de Sinners etUne bataille après l'autre remportera l’Oscar du meilleur film, avec un avantage marqué pour ce dernier.
Le site Gold Derby, largement considéré comme une des sources les plus fiables pour les prédictions en vue des Oscars, le plaçait en tête samedi avec 76,2 % de chances de l’emporter, contre 21,5 % pour Sinners.
Le site Polymarket, une plateforme qui permet aux internautes de parier sur des événements aussi variés que l’issue des conflits au Moyen-Orient ou les fluctuations des marchés financiers, affichait samedi la même tendance avec 76 % des paris placés pour Une bataille après l’autre et 21 % pour Sinners.
Michael B. Jordan et Miles Caton dans le film Sinners de Ryan Coogler.
Photo : Site web de Warner Bros. Canada
Les autres longs métrages en lice pour l’Oscar du meilleur film sont Hamnet, Bugonia, Marty Supreme, F1, L’agent secret, Valeur sentimentale, Frankenstein et Train Dreams, mais peu de spécialistes se sont aventurés à les placer en tête de leurs prédictions.
Du côté de l’Oscar du meilleur réalisateur, l’avantage penche aussi du côté de Paul Thomas Anderson, qui l’emporte presque systématiquement contre Ryan Coogler dans les pronostics.
Cette lutte à deux laisse peu de place aux autres cinéastes en lice : Chloé Zhao pour Hamnet, Josh Safdie pour Marty Supreme et Joachim Trier pour Valeur sentimentale.
Sinners et Une bataille après l’autre sont également favoris pour les Oscars respectifs du meilleur scénario original et du meilleur scénario adapté.
En se basant sur une formule mathématique qui prend en compte les récompenses déjà remises au cours de l’année et les tendances historiques, The Hollywood Reporter leur accorde des chances de 73,8 % et de 84,1 % dans leurs catégories respectives.
L'actrice irlandaise Jessie Buckley a remporté le prix de la meilleure actrice aux BAFTA, l'équivalent britannique des Oscars, pour son rôle d'Agnes Shakespeare dans Hamnet.
Photo : afp via getty images / JUSTIN TALLIS
Michael B. Jordan et Jessie Buckley favoris chez les acteurs
Du côté des prestigieux Oscars du meilleur acteur et de la meilleure actrice, deux grands favoris se démarquent dans les prédictions des spécialistes : Jordan B. Michael pour son double rôle des jumeaux Elijah et Elias dans Sinners ainsi que Jessie Buckley pour sa prestation très remarquée dans la peau d’Agnes Shakespeare dans Hamnet.
Certaines publications donnent aussi des chances à Timothée Chalamet chez les hommes pour son rôle du pongiste Marty Mauser dans Marty Supreme, par exemple le site Gold Derby, qui estimait ses chances à 26 % samedi.
Rappelons que cet acteur franco-américain a remporté le prix du meilleur acteur dans un film musical ou dans une comédie pour ce même rôle aux Golden Globes, mais son aura a depuis lors pâli après ses récents commentaires sur l’opéra et le ballet.
Dans une conversation avec Matthew McConaughey (nouvelle fenêtre) enregistrée le 24 février dernier par Variety et CNN, Timothée Chalamet s’est moqué de ces deux disciplines alors qu’il parlait de la survie du cinéma dans les salles.
Timothée Chalamet au moment de poser avec son trophée aux Golden Globes le 11 janvier 2026.
Photo : Reuters / Mario Anzuoni
Je ne veux pas travailler dans le ballet ou dans l’opéra, des choses où on dit : "Hé, gardons ça en vie, même si plus personne ne s’y intéresse vraiment"
, a-t-il confié à son partenaire d’Interstellar. Semblant se rendre rapidement compte de sa maladresse, il a ajouté : Tout mon respect pour toutes les personnes qui travaillent dans le ballet et l’opéra.
Ces commentaires lui ont valu les foudres de plusieurs personnes du milieu du ballet et de l’opéra, notamment du Metropolitan Opera de New York et de La Scala de Milan, ainsi que de collègues à Hollywood, dont Jamie Lee Curtis.
Vous avez envie d'y aller de votre propre pronostic pour dimanche soir? Rejoignez notre conversation en ligne et dites-nous vos prédictions. (nouvelle fenêtre)
Toutefois, cet incident ne devrait pas avoir de répercussions sur ses chances de remporter l’Oscar puisque l’essentiel des réactions négatives ont été rendues publiques la semaine dernière, après la fermeture du vote finale pour les Oscars par les membres de l’Académie, le 5 mars.
Les spécialistes donnent peu de chances à Leonardo DiCaprio, vedette d’Une bataille après l’autre, qui ne risque donc pas de reproduire sa victoire en 2016 pour The Revenant.
Amy Madigan est la favorite pour l’Oscar de la meilleure actrice dans un second rôle pour son incarnation terrifiante de Gladys Lilly dans le film d’horreur Évanouis (Weapons), alors que Sean Penn s’illustre du côté des hommes pour son rôle du colonel Steven J. Lockjaw dans Une bataille après l’autre.
Delroy Lindo (Sinners) est également pressenti pour l’Oscar du meilleur acteur dans un second rôle.
Amy Madigan dans le rôle de Gladys Lilly dans le film Weapons.
Photo : Page Instagram du film Weapons
Deux films québécois dans la course
Rappelons également que deux œuvres québécoises se retrouvent en lice aux Oscars cette année. La jeune fille qui pleurait des perles, réalisé par les Montréalais Chris Lavis et Maciek Szczerbowski, pourrait l’emporter dans la catégorie du meilleur court métrage d’animation.
Le film Perfectly a Strangeness, signé par Alison McAlpine, une réalisatrice originaire de Vancouver qui vit à Montréal, est de son côté en nomination pour l’Oscar du meilleur court métrage documentaire.
Ce film sans dialogues suit trois ânes qui découvrent un observatoire astronomique dans le désert d'Atacama, au Chili, et mise sur les sons, la musique et les images cristallines du ciel étoilé pour plonger le spectateur dans une rêverie contemplative à hauteur de quadrupèdes.
Pour ce qui est de l’Oscar du meilleur film international, la lutte se fera entre L'agent secret de Kleber Mendonça Filho (Brésil), Un simple accident de Jafar Panahi (France), Valeur sentimentale de Joachim Trier (Norvège), Sirāt d’Óliver Laxe (Espagne) et La voix de Hind Rajab de Kaouther Ben Hania (Tunisie).
Le court métrage La jeune fille qui pleurait des perles a été réalisé en animation image par image avec des marionnettes fabriquées à la main.
Photo : ONF
Un nouvel Oscar et de nouvelles règles
Un nouveau prix attendu depuis des années sera décerné pour la première fois dimanche : l’Oscar de la meilleure distribution, qui récompensera le travail peu connu des directeurs et directrices de distribution. Il s’agit du premier ajout de catégorie depuis celle du meilleur film d’animation, en 2001, ce qui porte le total de statuettes remises durant la soirée à 24.
La compétition se jouera entre Nina Gold (Hamnet), Jennifer Venditti (Marty Supreme), Cassandra Kulukundis (Une bataille après l’autre), Gabriel Domingues (L’agent secret) et Francine Maisler (Sinners).
Autre changement important : pour voter au tour final dans une catégorie spécifique, les membres de l’Académie devaient avoir visionné tous les films nommés dans cette catégorie. Ce qui n’était auparavant qu’une recommandation est maintenant une condition clairement inscrite dans le règlement.
La Britannique Nina Gold deviendra peut-être dimanche la première lauréate de l'Oscar de la meilleure distribution de rôles.
Photo : Getty Images / Monica Schipper
L’Académie a aussi clarifié dans ses nouvelles règles ce qui a trait à l’IA générative et à d'autres outils numériques, qui ne doivent ni avantager ni nuire aux chances d’un film à l’étape des nominations.
L'Académie et chaque section évalueront la performance en tenant compte de la place centrale qu'occupe l'humain dans la création au moment du choix du film à récompenser
, a expliqué l’Académie des arts et des sciences du cinéma au printemps 2025.
L’an dernier, l’Académie a également annoncé une nouvelle catégorie pour la conception des cascades, mais ce prix ne sera décerné qu’à compter de 2028.
Conan O’Brien de retour à l’animation
La 98e cérémonie des Oscars a lieu dimanche à compter de 19 h au Dolby Theatre à Los Angeles. L’humoriste et animateur de talk-show Conan O'Brien est de retour aux commandes du gala pour une deuxième année d'affilée.
Il sera entouré de plusieurs acteurs pour remettre les 24 statuettes, dont Javier Bardem, Chris Evans, Chase Infiniti, Demi Moore, Kumail Nanjiani et Maya Rudolph.
Les téléspectateurs auront aussi droit à des prestations musicales articulées autour des films Kpop Demon Hunters, en lice pour le meilleur film d’animation, et Sinners.
Conan O'Brien à l'animation de la 97e cérémonie des Oscars, le 2 mars 2025.
Photo : Getty Images / Kevin Winter
Le premier segment résonnera aux voix du groupe fictif de K-Pop HUNTR/X, qu’on peut voir dans le film, alors qu’elles interpréteront la chanson-thème Golden, en nomination pour l’Oscar de la meilleure chanson originale.
Le segment Sinners mettra en lumière le rôle de la musique dans la narration de ce film avec un hommage à son style visuel.
Miles Caton et Raphael Saadiq interpréteront la chanson I Lied To You, également en lice pour un Oscar, accompagnés de Misty Copeland, Eric Gales, Buddy Guy, Brittany Howard, Christone Kingfish
Ingram, Jayme Lawson, Li Jun Li, Bobby Rush, Shaboozey et Alice Smith.
La cérémonie sera diffusée en direct sur ABC et sur la plateforme Hulu aux États-Unis. Au Canada, la diffusion en direct est prévue sur la chaîne, sur le site et sur l’application de CTV, de même que sur Crave avec un abonnement.
